rules.legal_concept: Right of every person to examine and copy public records
rules.atomic_rule: Any person has the right to examine and take a copy of any public record of the state (no enumerated requester class), subject to statutory exemptions.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional right)
rules.source_language: Every person has a right to examine and take a copy of any public record of this state
rules.notes: Universal-access fact emitted as a rule per contract. Note: Idaho differentiates residents vs. nonresidents on fees (74-102) and response deadlines (74-103), but the underlying right to examine extends to every person.

rules.legal_concept: Custodian shall make no inquiry of requester (limited exceptions)
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian shall make no inquiry of any person who requests a public record, except to verify identity, to ensure records are not used for prohibited mailing/telephone number lists, or to protect personal information as allowed by law.
rules.trigger: Person requests a public record
rules.source_language: The custodian shall make no inquiry of any person who requests a public record, except [for identity verification, to ensure records are not used for prohibited mailing/telephone lists, or to protect personal information as provided by law]
rules.notes: Verbatim lead clause captured; the bracketed exceptions are the statutory 'except' list (identity, mailing/telephone list prohibition, personal-information protection). No statement-of-purpose may be required, but a residency attestation IS required (ID-0007), which is a permitted inquiry.

rules.legal_concept: Presumption that public records are open
rules.atomic_rule: Public records are presumed to be open and available for examination at all reasonable times, except as expressly prohibited or exempted by statute.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: presumption that records are open [at all reasonable times] except as prohibited by statute (paraphrased from 74-102 opening provision)
rules.notes: Paraphrase: could open the section but the retrieved text summarized the opening presumption clause rather than reproducing it verbatim; flag for verbatim re-capture of the exact 74-102(1) presumption language.

rules.legal_concept: Requests made to the designated custodian
rules.atomic_rule: All requests to examine public records shall be made to the designated custodian of such records as defined in section 74-101(3).
rules.trigger: Requester submits a request
rules.source_language: All requests to examine public records shall be made to the designated custodian of such records as defined in section 74-101(3), Idaho Code
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: drives routing. 'Custodian' = the person(s) having personal custody and control of the records (74-101(3)). The Act references an existing custodian rather than mandating a formally designated FOIA officer.

rules.legal_concept: Request must clearly indicate it is a public records request
rules.atomic_rule: A request must clearly indicate that it is a public records request.
rules.trigger: Requester submits a request
rules.source_language: clearly indicate that it is a public records request
rules.notes: Intake gating condition; the response clock (ID-0008/0009) attaches once a compliant request is received.

rules.legal_concept: Written request describing subject matter, records sought, and date range
rules.atomic_rule: The requester must submit a written request describing the subject matter, the records sought, and the specific date range, together with the requester's name, mailing address, email address, and telephone number.
rules.trigger: Requester submits a request
rules.source_language: Requests must submit written requests describing subject matter, records sought, and specific date ranges [and provide the requester's name, mailing address, email address, telephone number] (paraphrased from 74-102)
rules.notes: Paraphrase flagged: retrieved text summarized the description/contact requirement; needs verbatim re-capture of the exact 74-102 subsection listing required request contents. The contact/name/attestation portion was captured verbatim under ID-0007.

rules.legal_concept: Written declaration of residency status under oath
rules.atomic_rule: The request must include the requester's name, mailing address, email address, telephone number, and a written declaration, attesting or affirming under oath, whether the requester is a resident.
rules.trigger: Requester submits a request
rules.source_language: provide the requester's name, mailing address, email address, telephone number, and a written declaration by the requesting party attesting or affirming under oath whether such requester is a resident
rules.notes: State-specific fork introduced by the 2025 amendment: the sworn residency declaration determines which response-deadline tier (3 working days vs. 21 days) and which fee tier (resident free allotments vs. nonresident actual-cost) apply. 'Resident' = domicile in Idaho continuously >=30 days (74-101(15)).

rules.legal_concept: Grant or deny within 3 working days (resident)
rules.atomic_rule: A public agency or custodian shall either grant or deny a resident's request to examine or copy public records within three (3) working days of receipt of the request.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a resident's request
rules.clock_spec: fixed: 3 working-days from receipt of request (resident)
rules.source_language: A public agency or custodian shall either grant or deny a resident's request to examine or copy public records within three (3) working days of the date of the receipt of the request
rules.notes: Resident tier. Same concept as nonresident window (ID-0009); split by requester tier, not concept. Extendable under ID-0010.

rules.legal_concept: Grant or deny within 21 days (nonresident)
rules.atomic_rule: A public agency or custodian shall either grant or deny a request from a person who is not a resident and not employed by a resident to examine or copy public records within twenty-one (21) days of receipt of the request.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a nonresident's request
rules.clock_spec: fixed: 21 calendar-days from receipt of request (nonresident)
rules.source_language: A public agency or custodian shall either grant or deny a request from a person who is not a resident and not employed by a resident to examine or copy public records within twenty-one (21) days of the date of the receipt
rules.notes: Nonresident tier (2025 amendment). Extendable under ID-0011. Unit appears to be calendar days (contrast the resident 'working days' window).

rules.legal_concept: Extension to 10 working days to locate/retrieve (resident)
rules.atomic_rule: If a longer period is needed to locate or retrieve the records, the public agency shall provide the public records no later than ten (10) working days following a resident's request.
rules.trigger: Longer time needed to locate or retrieve the records
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: no later than 10 working-days from resident's request
rules.source_language: the public agency shall provide the public records no later than ten (10) working days following the person's request, if such person is a resident
rules.notes: Extension of the resident 3-working-day base window (ID-0008), triggered when records must be located or retrieved.

rules.legal_concept: Extension to 35 days to locate/retrieve (nonresident)
rules.atomic_rule: If a longer period is needed to locate or retrieve the records, the public agency shall provide the public records no later than thirty-five (35) days following a nonresident's request.
rules.trigger: Longer time needed to locate or retrieve the records
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: no later than 35 calendar-days from nonresident's request
rules.source_language: no later than thirty-five (35) days following a request from a nonresident
rules.notes: Extension of the nonresident 21-day base window (ID-0009).

rules.legal_concept: Electronic-format conversion extension with written notice and mutually agreed time
rules.atomic_rule: If an existing electronic record must first be converted to another electronic format and the conversion cannot be completed within the response time allotted, the agency shall so notify the requester in writing and provide the converted record at a time mutually agreed upon between the agency and the requester.
rules.trigger: Requested electronic record must be converted to another format and conversion cannot be completed within the allotted response time
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "mutually agreed upon" time from written conversion notice
rules.source_language: Additionally, if it is determined that the existing electronic record requested will first have to be converted to another electronic format by the agency or by a third party and that such conversion cannot be completed within the time allotted for the response, the agency shall so notify in writing the person requesting to examine or copy the records. The agency shall provide the converted public record at a time mutually agreed upon between the agency and the requester, with due consideration given to any limitations that may exist due to the process of conversion or due to the use of a third party to make the conversion.
rules.notes: Soft deadline: no numeric period; requires written notice plus a mutually agreed delivery time -> config_home structural per contract. Distinct sub-path from the ordinary locate/retrieve extension (ID-0010/0011).

rules.legal_concept: Failure to timely respond deemed a denial
rules.atomic_rule: If the public agency or custodian fails to respond within the time allotted for the response, the request shall be deemed to be denied.
rules.trigger: No response within the allotted response time
rules.clock_spec: terminal: deemed denial at expiry of the applicable response window (ID-0008/0009, or extension ID-0010/0011)
rules.source_language: If the public agency or custodian fails to respond within the time allotted for the response, the request shall be deemed to be denied.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: constructive-denial trigger. The deemed denial starts the appeal path; the 180-day judicial petition clock (ID-0028) runs from the date of mailing of a notice of denial.

rules.legal_concept: Written notice of denial or partial denial
rules.atomic_rule: On a denial or partial denial, the person legally responsible for administering the public agency or that person's designee shall notify the person in writing of the denial or partial denial.
rules.trigger: Agency denies or partially denies a request
rules.source_language: the person legally responsible for administering the public agency or that person's designee shall notify the person in writing of the denial or partial denial
rules.notes: Required document on denial. Routes the denial to a named responsible official/designee.

rules.legal_concept: Contents of denial notice: statutory authority and appeal rights/time periods
rules.atomic_rule: The notice of denial or partial denial shall indicate the statutory authority for the denial and clearly indicate the person's right to appeal the denial or partial denial and the time periods for doing so.
rules.trigger: Agency issues a written denial or partial denial
rules.source_language: The notice of denial or partial denial...shall indicate the statutory authority for the denial and indicate clearly the person's right to appeal the denial or partial denial and the time periods for doing so.
rules.notes: Retrieved text also indicated the notice reflects attorney-review status; capture of that specific clause deferred for verbatim confirmation. Notice must state the appeal time period, which corresponds to the 180-day judicial petition window (ID-0028).

rules.legal_concept: Separation of exempt and nonexempt material
rules.atomic_rule: If a record contains both nonexempt and exempt material, the agency shall, upon receipt of a request, separate the exempt and nonexempt material and make the nonexempt material available for examination; a request to copy nonexempt material may not be denied merely because it is contained in the same record as exempt material.
rules.trigger: Record contains both exempt and nonexempt material and a request is received
rules.source_language: If any public record contains material which is not exempt from disclosure as well as material which is exempt from disclosure, the public agency shall, upon receipt of a request for disclosure, separate the exempt and nonexempt material and make the nonexempt material available for examination, provided that a denial of a request to copy nonexempt material in a public record shall not be based upon the fact that such nonexempt material is contained in the same public record as the exempt material.
rules.notes: Full verbatim text captured.

rules.legal_concept: First 2 hours of labor free (resident)
rules.atomic_rule: No fee shall be charged for the first two (2) hours of labor in responding to a resident's public records request.
rules.trigger: Resident request; labor incurred
rules.source_language: no fee shall be charged for the first two (2) hours of labor in responding to a request submitted by a resident for public records, or for copying the first one hundred (100) pages
rules.notes: Resident-only free allotment. Split from the free-copies allotment (ID-0018) which shares the same source sentence.

rules.legal_concept: First 100 pages of copies free (resident)
rules.atomic_rule: No fee shall be charged for copying the first one hundred (100) pages of paper records in responding to a resident's request.
rules.trigger: Resident request; copies made
rules.source_language: no fee shall be charged for the first two (2) hours of labor in responding to a request submitted by a resident for public records, or for copying the first one hundred (100) pages
rules.notes: Resident-only free allotment; charges above the threshold governed by the actual-cost ceiling (ID-0019).

rules.legal_concept: Copy fee may not exceed actual cost (resident)
rules.atomic_rule: The fee charged to a resident may not exceed the actual cost to the agency of copying the record.
rules.trigger: Copies provided beyond the free allotment
rules.source_language: The fee for residents may not exceed the actual cost to the agency of copying the record
rules.notes: Idaho sets no statutory per-page cents rate; the ceiling is 'actual cost' (city supplies the operative rate under it).

rules.legal_concept: Labor charges limited to reasonable cost at lowest-paid staff rate
rules.atomic_rule: Fees for resident requests shall not exceed reasonable labor costs necessarily incurred, charged at the per-hour pay rate of the lowest-paid administrative staff employee or public official of the agency.
rules.trigger: Labor incurred beyond the free 2-hour allotment
rules.source_language: Fees for requests made by residents shall not exceed reasonable labor costs necessarily incurred in responding to a public records request ... shall be charged at the per hour pay rate of the lowest paid administrative staff employee or public official of the public agency
rules.notes: Two verbatim fragments from 74-102(10)(e) joined; the labor rate is bound to a specific staff pay rate (city supplies the actual dollar rate under the ceiling).

rules.legal_concept: Computer/electronic record fee capped at sum of enumerated costs
rules.atomic_rule: For computer records, the agency may charge a fee that does not exceed the sum of the direct cost of copying, the standard cost of publication, and the cost of conversion.
rules.trigger: Request for records maintained in a computer/electronic system
rules.source_language: a public agency or public official may charge a fee...that does not exceed the sum of [direct cost of copying, standard cost of publication, and cost of conversion]
rules.notes: Verbatim lead clause captured with ellipsis; the three enumerated cost components should be re-captured verbatim from 74-102(10)(d) for the exact list.

rules.legal_concept: Nonresident fees may be higher but not exceed actual cost
rules.atomic_rule: The agency may charge nonresidents higher fees than residents (including for labor and copies without the resident free allotments), but such fees may not exceed the actual cost to the agency.
rules.trigger: Nonresident request
rules.source_language: Agencies may charge higher fees for non-residents, though fees cannot exceed actual costs (paraphrased from 74-102)
rules.notes: Paraphrase flagged: retrieved text summarized the nonresident fee treatment; needs verbatim re-capture of the exact 74-102(10) nonresident subsection. Core fork: nonresidents do not receive the resident free-labor/free-copy allotments.

rules.legal_concept: Fee waiver in the public interest for indigent resident requester
rules.atomic_rule: The agency shall not charge a resident any cost or fee for copies or labor when the examination is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding, is not primarily in the individual interest of the requester, and the requester lacks sufficient financial resources such that fees would prevent access.
rules.trigger: Resident requester meets the public-interest and inability-to-pay conditions
rules.source_language: The public agency shall not charge any cost or fee for copies or labor when the requester is a resident [and the examination is likely to contribute to public understanding, is not primarily in the individual interest, and fees would prevent access due to insufficient resources]
rules.notes: Verbatim lead clause captured; the three-part waiver test in brackets was summarized and should be re-captured verbatim. Waiver limited to residents. Multi-factor conjunctive standard kept in one row per grain rule.

rules.legal_concept: Custodian may require advance payment of fees
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian may require advance payment of the fees authorized by this section before providing the records.
rules.trigger: Fees are authorized for the request
rules.source_language: The custodian may require advance payment of fees authorized by this section
rules.notes: Discretionary ('may'); permits an advance-payment/deposit gate on production.

rules.legal_concept: Electronic-format copy if available and specifically requested
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may provide a copy of a public record in electronic form if the record is available in electronic form and the person specifically requests an electronic copy.
rules.trigger: Record available in electronic form and requester specifically requests electronic copy
rules.source_language: Nothing contained herein shall prevent a public agency from providing a copy of a public record in electronic form if the record is available in electronic form and if the person specifically requests an electronic copy
rules.notes: Permissive format-provision rule; interacts with the conversion extension (ID-0012) and electronic-record fee (ID-0021).

rules.legal_concept: Records open for inspection at all reasonable times
rules.atomic_rule: Public records shall be open for inspection and copying at all reasonable times, and the agency shall provide reasonable opportunity to inspect or copy on demand.
rules.trigger: Request to inspect
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "at all reasonable times" for inspection availability
rules.source_language: records are open [for inspection] during reasonable times ... provide certified copies or reasonable inspection/copying opportunities on demand (paraphrased from 74-102)
rules.notes: Paraphrase flagged: 'reasonable times' is a soft standard -> config_home structural, no numeric value. Needs verbatim re-capture of the exact 74-102 inspection-availability clause.

rules.legal_concept: Petition to district court to enforce right to examine
rules.atomic_rule: A person denied the right to examine or copy records may institute proceedings in the district court of the county where the records or some part thereof are located.
rules.trigger: Denial (actual or deemed) of a request
rules.source_language: institute proceedings in the district court of the county where the records or some part thereof are located
rules.notes: Judicial appeal path (namespaced appeal.judicial). The Idaho Public Records Act provides no internal administrative appeal stage; review is by district-court petition. Burden-of-proof / in-camera / de-novo clauses not located in retrieved 74-115 text (see material negatives).

rules.legal_concept: 180-day deadline to file district-court petition
rules.atomic_rule: The petition to the district court must be filed within one hundred eighty (180) calendar days from the date of mailing of the notice of denial.
rules.trigger: Mailing of the notice of denial
rules.clock_spec: fixed: 180 calendar-days from date of mailing of notice of denial
rules.source_language: filed within one hundred eighty (180) calendar days from the date of mailing of the notice of denial
rules.notes: Statute-of-limitations style deadline (fixed). Runs from mailing of the denial notice; the denial notice must disclose this time period (ID-0015).

structural_branches.description: The 2025 amendment (ch. 298) creates a resident vs. nonresident fork determined by a sworn residency declaration (ID-0007): residents get a 3-working-day response window and free allotments (2 labor hours / 100 pages); nonresidents get a 21-day window and no free allotments. The engine must branch every request on residency status.

Distinct electronic-format conversion sub-path (ID-0012): when a record must be converted and cannot be delivered in the allotted time, the agency issues a written notice and delivers at a mutually agreed time -- a bespoke soft-deadline stage separate from the ordinary locate/retrieve extension.
Nonresponse within the allotted window is a terminal deemed-denial state (ID-0013) that ends normal processing and opens the judicial appeal path.
Idaho's Act provides only a judicial appeal path -- petition to district court (ID-0027) within 180 days (ID-0028). There is no internal/administrative appeal stage to model.

material_negatives.note: Idaho sets NO statutory per-page cents copy rate. Copy fees are bound only to 'actual cost' (74-102(10)(c)); the city supplies the operative rate under that ceiling.
No separate acknowledgment-of-receipt requirement found; the statute requires the agency to 'grant or deny' within the response window (74-103), not a distinct acknowledgment.

No explicit clarification clock or nonresponse-abandonment provision located in Title 74 Ch. 1. The 'clearly indicate it is a public records request' requirement (ID-0005) is the closest intake gate; absence of a clarification rule is not proof none exists.

The retrieved 74-115 text did not include an explicit burden-of-proof-on-agency, in-camera-examination, or de-novo-review clause. Requires manual verification of the full 74-115 text before asserting or excluding these.
Idaho does not appear to require formally designating/publishing a public-records officer; it references the existing 'custodian' (74-101(3)). Contrast IL/WA which mandate an officer designation.

Idaho Code 74-113 (Access to Records About a Person by a Person) creates a distinct access-to-own-records workflow, and 74-120 prohibits use of records for mailing/telephone lists (driving the permitted custodian inquiry). Not fully captured this pass; flag for a special-records / distinct-workflow follow-up.

Resident windows are stated in 'working days' (3 / 10) while nonresident windows are stated in plain 'days' (21 / 35). Whether nonresident days are calendar days (assumed here) should be confirmed against the exact 74-103(2) text.

rules.legal_concept: Right to inspect a public record free of charge
rules.atomic_rule: Any person has the right to inspect a public record free of charge and to take a copy during normal working hours, subject to the fee and response sections.
rules.trigger: None stated (any person)
rules.source_language: Except as provided in Subsection (1)(b), a person has the right to inspect a public record free of charge, and the right to take a copy of a public record during normal working hours, subject to Sections 63G-2-203 and 63G-2-204.
rules.notes: Config_home marked parameter only to satisfy schema; substantively this is the universal-access grant. Exceptions in 201(1)(b): already-provided copies, non-fillable requests under 7(a)(v), and non-segregable electronic files.

rules.legal_concept: No residency/citizenship condition on access
rules.atomic_rule: The right of access runs to 'a person' with no residency or citizenship qualification imposed by GRAMA.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: GRAMA grants the right of inspection and copying to 'a person' (§ 63G-2-201(1)(a)) and § 63G-2-204(1)(a) enumerates the required contents of a request without any residency or citizenship element; no provision conditions access on residency.
rules.notes: is_paraphrase=true: GRAMA has no explicit no-residency clause; this is the universal-access symmetry fact stated from the affirmative 'a person' grant and the absence of a residency element in the request-content list. Requires manual verification.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required
rules.atomic_rule: A requester need not state a reason or purpose; purpose is not among the required contents of a records request.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: The required contents of a written request under § 63G-2-204(1)(a) are the requester's name, mailing address, email address (if applicable), daytime telephone number, and a description of the record with reasonable specificity; no statement of purpose is required (purpose is relevant only to optional expedited response and fee waivers).
rules.notes: is_paraphrase=true: inferred from the absence of purpose in the mandatory request-content list. Note purpose IS optionally relevant to expedited-response benefit (204(4)-(5)) and fee waivers (203(4)); those are separate rules. Requires manual verification.

rules.legal_concept: Written request required
rules.atomic_rule: A person requesting a record must submit a written request to the governmental entity that retains the record.
rules.trigger: Person seeks a record
rules.source_language: A person making a request for a record shall submit to the governmental entity that retains the record a written request containing: (i) the person's: (A) name; (B) mailing address; (C) email address, if the person has an email address and is willing to accept communications by email relating to the person's records request; and (D) daytime telephone number; and (ii) a description of the record requested that identifies the record with reasonable specificity.
rules.notes: Enumerated required fields: name, mailing address, email (if applicable), daytime telephone, and reasonably-specific description. Split into UT-0005 (specificity standard).

rules.legal_concept: Reasonable specificity of record description
rules.atomic_rule: The request's description must identify the record with reasonable specificity.
rules.trigger: Written request submitted
rules.source_language: a description of the record requested that identifies the record with reasonable specificity.
rules.notes: 'Reasonable specificity' is an undefined soft standard, not a numeric parameter. GRAMA states no formal clarification-clock or nonresponse-abandonment procedure (see material negatives).

rules.legal_concept: One request may not span multiple entities
rules.atomic_rule: A single record request may not be submitted to multiple governmental entities (though identical separate requests to each entity are allowed).
rules.trigger: Request submitted
rules.source_language: (i) A single record request may not be submitted to multiple governmental entities. (ii) Subsection (1)(b)(i) may not be construed to prevent a person from submitting a separate record request to each of multiple governmental entities, even if each of the separate requests seeks access to the same record.

rules.legal_concept: Entity may specify where requests are directed
rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity may make rules specifying where and to whom requests for access must be directed.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: A governmental entity may make rules in accordance with Title 63G, Chapter 3, Utah Administrative Rulemaking Act, specifying where and to whom requests for access shall be directed.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: drives routing / custodian designation.

rules.legal_concept: Prompt forwarding of misdirected request; clock start
rules.atomic_rule: If a request goes to the wrong office, that office must promptly forward it to the appropriate office; if promptly forwarded, the response clock starts when the correct office receives it.
rules.trigger: Request submitted to office other than the one specified by rule
rules.clock_spec: response time limit begins when request is received by the office specified by rule
rules.source_language: (a) If a request for access is submitted to an office of a governmental entity other than that specified by rule in accordance with Subsection (3), the office shall promptly forward the request to the appropriate office. (b) If the request is forwarded promptly, the time limit for response begins when the request is received by the office specified by rule.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver #1 (routing). Clock-start rule for the 10/5-business-day response window.

rules.legal_concept: Time for responding to a records request
rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity must respond (approve/provide, deny, disclaim custody, or claim extraordinary circumstances) as soon as reasonably possible but no later than 10 business days after receiving a written request.
rules.trigger: Receipt of written request
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 10 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: After receiving a request for a record, a governmental entity shall: ... (b) as soon as reasonably possible, but no later than 10 business days after receiving a written request, or five business days after receiving a written request if the requester demonstrates that expedited response to the record request benefits the public rather than the person: (i) approve the request and provide a copy of the record; (ii) deny the request in accordance with the procedures and requirements of Section 63G-2-205; (iii) notify the requester that it does not maintain the record requested and provide, if known, the name and address of the governmental entity that does maintain the record; or (iv) notify the requester that because of one of the extraordinary circumstances listed in Subsection (6), it cannot immediately approve or deny the request...
rules.notes: 'as soon as reasonably possible' is a soft floor on top of the 10-business-day hard ceiling. Political subdivisions may set different response times under § 63G-2-701(4)(b) if resources are insufficient (see UT-0049).

rules.legal_concept: Expedited (5-business-day) response
rules.atomic_rule: If the requester demonstrates that an expedited response benefits the public rather than the person, the entity must respond no later than 5 business days after receiving the request.
rules.trigger: Requester demonstrates expedited response benefits the public rather than the person
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 5 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: or five business days after receiving a written request if the requester demonstrates that expedited response to the record request benefits the public rather than the person

rules.legal_concept: Notice that expedited treatment is denied
rules.atomic_rule: For a request seeking expedited response, the entity must review it and, within 5 business days, notify any requester who has not demonstrated public benefit that the response will not be expedited.
rules.trigger: Request seeks expedited response but public benefit not demonstrated
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 5 business-days from request receipt
rules.source_language: After receiving a request for a record, a governmental entity shall: (a) review each request that seeks an expedited response and notify, within five business days after receiving the request, each requester that has not demonstrated that their record request benefits the public rather than the person that their response will not be expedited;

rules.legal_concept: Presumption that media requests benefit the public
rules.atomic_rule: A person who requests a record to obtain information for a story or report for publication or broadcast to the general public is presumed to act to benefit the public rather than a person.
rules.trigger: Request is for a story/report for publication or broadcast to the general public
rules.source_language: Any person who requests a record to obtain information for a story or report for publication or broadcast to the general public is presumed to be acting to benefit the public rather than a person.
rules.notes: Drives the expedited-response branch (UT-0010). Note: this publication/broadcast presumption is distinct from the narrower 'media representative' definition governing the fee exemption in § 63G-2-203(5) (which excludes blogs/podcasts).

rules.legal_concept: Notice that entity does not maintain the record
rules.atomic_rule: If the entity does not maintain the requested record, it must, within the response window, notify the requester and provide (if known) the name and address of the entity that does maintain it.
rules.trigger: Entity does not maintain the requested record
rules.source_language: notify the requester that it does not maintain the record requested and provide, if known, the name and address of the governmental entity that does maintain the record;
rules.notes: Routing/referral outcome; occurs within the UT-0009 window.

rules.legal_concept: Extraordinary-circumstances delay notice
rules.atomic_rule: If extraordinary circumstances prevent immediate approval or denial, the entity must, within the response window, notify the requester with a description of the circumstances and the date the records will be available.
rules.trigger: One of the enumerated extraordinary circumstances applies
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: extension period per Subsection (7), stated as a 'date when the records will be available'
rules.source_language: notify the requester that because of one of the extraordinary circumstances listed in Subsection (6), it cannot immediately approve or deny the request, and include with the notice: (A) a description of the circumstances that constitute the extraordinary circumstances; and (B) the date when the records will be available, consistent with the requirements of Subsection (7).
rules.notes: Structural branch: the request enters an extended-processing state. Extension length depends on which ground applies (UT-0015..UT-0018).

rules.legal_concept: Defined extraordinary circumstances
rules.atomic_rule: Only the eight enumerated circumstances (record in use by another entity; audit use; voluminous request; large volume of pending requests; large-volume review to locate; legal-counsel analysis needed; extensive editing to segregate; segregation requires programming) qualify as extraordinary circumstances permitting delay.
rules.trigger: Entity seeks to extend response time
rules.source_language: The following circumstances constitute "extraordinary circumstances" that allow a governmental entity to delay approval or denial by an additional period of time as specified in Subsection (7)...: (a) another governmental entity is using the record...; (b) another governmental entity is using the record as part of an audit...; (c)(i) the request is for a voluminous quantity of records or a record series containing a substantial number of records; or (ii) the requester seeks a substantial number of records or records series in requests filed within five working days of each other; (d) the governmental entity is currently processing a large number of records requests; (e) the request requires the governmental entity to review a large number of records to locate the records requested; (f) the decision to release a record involves legal issues that require the governmental entity to seek legal counsel...; (g) segregating information... requires extensive editing; or (h) segregating information... requires computer programming.
rules.notes: Enumerated closed list; kept as one row (conjunctive definition) per grain rule.

rules.legal_concept: Extension for legal-counsel analysis
rules.atomic_rule: Where the delay is due to legal-issue analysis requiring counsel, the entity must approve or deny within 5 business days after the original response time expired.
rules.trigger: Extraordinary circumstance under 204(6)(f)
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 5 business-days after the original response time expires
rules.source_language: for claims under Subsection (6)(f), the governmental entity shall either approve or deny the request within five business days after the response time specified for the original request has expired;

rules.legal_concept: Extension for extensive editing to segregate
rules.atomic_rule: Where segregating disclosable from non-disclosable information requires extensive editing, the entity must fulfill the request within 15 business days from the date of the original request.
rules.trigger: Extraordinary circumstance under 204(6)(g)
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 15 business-days from date of original request
rules.source_language: for claims under Subsection (6)(g), the governmental entity shall fulfill the request within 15 business days from the date of the original request; or

rules.legal_concept: Soft 'as soon as reasonably possible' extension for volume/programming grounds
rules.atomic_rule: For voluminous/high-volume/locate-review grounds and for grounds requiring computer programming, the entity must disclose located records the requester may inspect, give an estimate of time to finish, and complete and disclose as soon as reasonably possible.
rules.trigger: Extraordinary circumstance under 204(6)(c),(d),(e), or (h)
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "as soon as reasonably possible" from the extraordinary-circumstances notice
rules.source_language: for claims under Subsections (6)(c), (d), and (e), the governmental entity shall: (i) disclose the records that it has located which the requester is entitled to inspect; (ii) provide the requester with an estimate of the amount of time it will take to finish the work required to respond to the request; (iii) complete the work and disclose those records that the requester is entitled to inspect as soon as reasonably possible; ... (f) for claims under Subsection (6)(h), the governmental entity shall complete its programming and disclose the requested records as soon as reasonably possible.
rules.notes: Soft standard -> config_home structural per contract. Includes a duty to provide a time estimate.

rules.legal_concept: Failure to respond equals denial
rules.atomic_rule: If the entity fails to provide the records or issue a denial within the specified time period, that failure is deemed a determination denying access.
rules.trigger: No response or denial issued within the response deadline
rules.clock_spec: terminal event at expiry of the applicable response window (10 or 5 business-days)
rules.source_language: If the governmental entity fails to provide the requested records or issue a denial within the specified time period, that failure is considered the equivalent of a determination denying access to the record.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver #3: deemed/constructive denial trigger. Starts the 30-day appeal clock (UT-0040).

rules.legal_concept: Duty to conduct a reasonable search
rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity must conduct a reasonable search for a requested record.
rules.trigger: Record request received
rules.source_language: A governmental entity shall conduct a reasonable search for a requested record.
rules.notes: 'Reasonable' is an undefined soft standard; not a numeric parameter.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to create, compile, or reformat records
rules.atomic_rule: In responding, an entity is not required to create a record; compile/format/manipulate/package/summarize/tailor information; or provide a record in a format, medium, or program not currently maintained.
rules.trigger: Request would require creation/compilation/reformatting
rules.source_language: In response to a request, a governmental entity is not required to: (i) create a record; (ii) compile, format, manipulate, package, summarize, or tailor information; (iii) provide a record in a particular format, medium, or program not currently maintained by the governmental entity;
rules.notes: Entity MAY optionally do so under 201(8), and may charge for it under § 63G-2-203.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to fulfill unreasonably duplicative requests
rules.atomic_rule: An entity is not required to fulfill a request that unreasonably duplicates prior records requests from that same person.
rules.trigger: Request unreasonably duplicates prior requests from the same person
rules.source_language: fulfill a person's records request if the request unreasonably duplicates prior records requests from that person;

rules.legal_concept: No duty to fill request for records already publicly available
rules.atomic_rule: An entity need not fill a request where the record is publicly accessible online or in a public publication/product, provided the entity specifies where it is accessible or provides the publication and specifies where the record is found.
rules.trigger: Requested record is publicly accessible online or in a public publication
rules.source_language: fill a person's records request if: (A) the record requested is: (I) publicly accessible online; or (II) included in a public publication or product produced by the governmental entity receiving the request; and (B) the governmental entity: (I) specifies to the person requesting the record where the record is accessible online; or (II) provides the person requesting the record with the public publication or product and specifies where the record can be found...
rules.notes: Routing/refusal outcome conditioned on the entity pointing the requester to the source.

rules.legal_concept: Electronic copy in lieu of paper
rules.atomic_rule: An entity must provide an electronic copy in lieu of paper if the requester prefers electronic, the entity currently maintains a reproducible electronic format providable without reformatting/conversion, and the copy does not disclose exempt records or can be segregated without undue expenditure.
rules.trigger: Requester requests/prefers electronic copy and conditions met
rules.source_language: Subject to the requirements of Subsection (7), a governmental entity shall provide access to an electronic copy of a record in lieu of providing access to its paper equivalent if: (a) the person making the request requests or states a preference for an electronic copy; (b) the governmental entity currently maintains the record in an electronic format that is reproducible and may be provided without reformatting or conversion; and (c) the electronic copy of the record: (i) does not disclose other records that are exempt from disclosure; or (ii) may be segregated to protect private, protected, or controlled information from disclosure without the undue expenditure of public resources or funds.

rules.legal_concept: Physical form may not be used to deny access
rules.atomic_rule: An entity may not use the physical form (electronic or otherwise) in which a record is stored to deny or unreasonably hinder inspection or copying.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: A governmental entity may not use the physical form, electronic or otherwise, in which a record is stored to deny, or unreasonably hinder the rights of a person to inspect and receive a copy of a record under this chapter.

rules.legal_concept: Requester self-copying for large requests
rules.atomic_rule: For a request of more than 50 pages, an entity may allow the requester to make the copies (using entity facilities or the requester's own) where the files contain no exempt records or can be segregated and reasonable safeguards are provided.
rules.trigger: Request exceeds 50 pages and segregability/safeguard conditions met
rules.source_language: A governmental entity may allow a person requesting more than 50 pages of records to copy the records if: (i) the records are contained in files that do not contain records that are exempt from disclosure, or the records may be segregated to remove private, protected, or controlled information from disclosure; and (ii) the governmental entity provides reasonable safeguards to protect the public from the potential for loss of a public record.
rules.notes: 50-page threshold (floor: 'more than 50 pages'). If requester uses own facilities on-site, entity waives copying fees. Cross-referenced by extraordinary-circumstances handling in 204(7)(c)(iv).

rules.legal_concept: Certified copy of a record
rules.atomic_rule: An entity must provide a certified copy of a record if the person has a right to inspect it, identifies it with reasonable specificity, and pays the lawful fees.
rules.trigger: Requester with inspection right requests certified copy and pays fees
rules.source_language: A governmental entity shall provide a person with a certified copy of a record if: (a) the person requesting the record has a right to inspect it; (b) the person identifies the record with reasonable specificity; and (c) the person pays the lawful fees.

rules.legal_concept: Reasonable fee to cover actual cost
rules.atomic_rule: An entity may charge a reasonable fee to cover its actual cost of providing a record; the fee must be approved by the entity's executive officer.
rules.trigger: Entity provides a record
rules.source_language: (a) Subject to Subsection (5), a governmental entity may charge a reasonable fee to cover the governmental entity's actual cost of providing a record. (b) A fee under Subsection (1)(a) shall be approved by the governmental entity's executive officer.
rules.notes: Ceiling = actual cost; also bounded by the soft 'reasonable' standard. Executive-officer approval is a structural sub-requirement (UT-0030).

rules.legal_concept: Actual-cost components for compiled records
rules.atomic_rule: When compiling a record in a form other than normally maintained, actual costs may include staff time for compiling/formatting/tailoring, staff time for search/retrieval and direct administrative costs, and (for non-word-processing computer output) actual incremental cost plus a reasonable portion of formatting/administrative costs.
rules.trigger: Entity compiles a record in a form other than normally maintained
rules.source_language: When a governmental entity compiles a record in a form other than that normally maintained by the governmental entity, the actual costs under this section may include the following: (i) the cost of staff time for compiling, formatting, manipulating, packaging, summarizing, or tailoring the record...; (ii) the cost of staff time for search, retrieval, and other direct administrative costs for complying with a request; and (iii) in the case of fees for a record that is the result of computer output other than word processing, the actual incremental cost of providing the electronic services and products together with a reasonable portion of the costs associated with formatting or interfacing the information for particular users, and the administrative costs...

rules.legal_concept: Hourly charge capped at lowest-paid qualified employee
rules.atomic_rule: An hourly staff-time charge may not exceed the salary of the lowest paid employee who has the necessary skill and training to perform the request.
rules.trigger: Entity charges staff-time hourly fee
rules.source_language: An hourly charge under Subsection (2)(a) may not exceed the salary of the lowest paid employee who, in the discretion of the custodian of records, has the necessary skill and training to perform the request.

rules.legal_concept: Political subdivisions set fees by ordinance/policy
rules.atomic_rule: Political subdivisions must establish records fees by ordinance or written formal policy adopted by the governing body.
rules.trigger: Political subdivision establishes fees
rules.source_language: Political subdivisions shall establish fees by ordinance or written formal policy adopted by the governing body.
rules.notes: The municipal hook: the CITY supplies the actual fee schedule under the state's actual-cost ceiling (UT-0028).

rules.legal_concept: Discretionary fee waiver
rules.atomic_rule: An entity may (and is encouraged to) fulfill a request without charge if release primarily benefits the public, the requester is the subject of/specified in the record, or the requester's legal rights are directly implicated and the requester is impecunious.
rules.trigger: One of the enumerated benefit/subject/impecunious conditions
rules.source_language: A governmental entity may fulfill a record request without charge and is encouraged to do so if it determines that: (a) releasing the record primarily benefits the public rather than a person; (b) the individual requesting the record is the subject of the record, or an individual specified in Subsection 63G-2-202(1) or (2); or (c) the requester's legal rights are directly implicated by the information in the record, and the requester is impecunious.
rules.notes: Denial of a fee waiver is separately appealable (UT-0040) and reviewed de novo (§ 63G-2-203(6)).

rules.legal_concept: No fee for inspection
rules.atomic_rule: An entity may not charge a fee for inspecting a record.
rules.trigger: Requester inspects (does not copy) a record
rules.source_language: A governmental entity may not charge a fee for: ... (ii) inspecting a record;
rules.notes: Fixed at $0 for inspection.

rules.legal_concept: No fee for reviewing a record for disclosability
rules.atomic_rule: An entity may not charge a fee for reviewing a record to determine whether it is subject to disclosure, except as permitted for search/retrieval staff time under 203(2)(a)(ii).
rules.trigger: Entity reviews record for disclosability
rules.source_language: A governmental entity may not charge a fee for: (i) reviewing a record to determine whether it is subject to disclosure, except as permitted by Subsection (2)(a)(ii);

rules.legal_concept: First quarter hour of staff time free
rules.atomic_rule: An entity may not charge a fee for the first quarter hour of staff time spent responding to a request.
rules.trigger: Entity responds to a request under § 63G-2-204
rules.source_language: A governmental entity may not charge a fee for: ... (iii) the first quarter hour of staff time spent in responding to a request under Section 63G-2-204.
rules.notes: Fixed free allotment of 15 minutes. Exception in UT-0036.

rules.legal_concept: Exception to free first quarter hour for repeat non-media requesters
rules.atomic_rule: The free first quarter hour does not apply if the requester is not a Utah media representative AND previously submitted a separate request within the 10-day period immediately before the current request.
rules.trigger: Non-media requester filed a separate request within prior 10 days
rules.source_language: Notwithstanding Subsection (5)(b)(iii), a governmental entity is not prevented from charging a fee for the first quarter hour of staff time spent in responding to a request under Section 63G-2-204 if the person who submits the request: (i) is not a Utah media representative; and (ii) previously submitted a separate request within the 10-day period immediately before the date of the request to which the governmental entity is responding.
rules.notes: 'Media representative' here (203(5)(a)) excludes blog/podcast/social-media requesters, unlike the broader publication/broadcast presumption in 204(5).

rules.legal_concept: Advance payment before processing
rules.atomic_rule: An entity may require payment of past fees and future estimated fees before beginning to process a request.
rules.trigger: Fees expected to exceed $50, or prior invoiced fees unpaid
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: processing withheld until prepayment received ('before beginning to process a request')
rules.source_language: A governmental entity may require payment of past fees and future estimated fees before beginning to process a request if: (i) fees are expected to exceed $50; or (ii) after the government entity has sent an invoice, the requester has not paid fees from a previous request.
rules.notes: Prepayment gate; the request enters a hold state until paid. Threshold value in UT-0038.

rules.legal_concept: $50 prepayment threshold
rules.atomic_rule: Prepayment may be required when fees are expected to exceed $50.
rules.trigger: Estimated fees exceed $50
rules.source_language: fees are expected to exceed $50;
rules.notes: Fixed statutory threshold.

rules.legal_concept: Refund of excess prepayment
rules.atomic_rule: Any prepaid amount in excess of fees due must be returned to the requester.
rules.trigger: Prepaid amount exceeds fees actually due
rules.source_language: Any prepaid amount in excess of fees due shall be returned to the requester.

rules.legal_concept: Segregation of disclosable from non-disclosable information
rules.atomic_rule: If a record contains both disclosable and non-disclosable information and the disclosable portion is intelligible, the entity must allow access to the disclosable information and may deny the exempt information by issuing a notice of denial.
rules.trigger: Record contains both entitled and non-entitled information
rules.source_language: if a governmental entity receives a request for access to a record that contains both information that the requester is entitled to inspect and information that the requester is not entitled to inspect under this chapter, and, if the information the requester is entitled to inspect is intelligible, the governmental entity: (1) shall, except as provided in Subsection 63G-2-201(1)(b)(iii), allow access to information in the record that the requester is entitled to inspect under this chapter; and (2) may deny access to information in the record if the information is exempt from disclosure to the requester, issuing a notice of denial as provided in Section 63G-2-205.
rules.notes: Partial-denial of segregated portions triggers the denial-notice machinery (UT-0044).

rules.legal_concept: Notice of denial
rules.atomic_rule: If the entity denies a request in whole or part, it must provide a notice of denial to the requester either in person or by sending it to the requester's address.
rules.trigger: Request denied in whole or part
rules.source_language: If the governmental entity denies the request in whole or part, it shall provide a notice of denial to the requester either in person or by sending the notice to the requester's address.

rules.legal_concept: Required contents of denial notice
rules.atomic_rule: The notice of denial must contain a description of the denied record/portions, citations to the exempting provisions, a statement of the right to appeal to the chief administrative officer, and the appeal time limits plus the CAO's name and business address.
rules.trigger: Notice of denial issued
rules.source_language: The notice of denial shall contain the following information: (a) a description of the record or portions of the record to which access was denied...; (b) citations to the provisions of this chapter, court rule or order, another state statute, federal statute, or federal regulation that exempt the record or portions of the record from disclosure...; (c) a statement that the requester has the right to appeal the denial to the chief administrative officer of the governmental entity; and (d) the time limits for filing an appeal, and the name and business address of the chief administrative officer of the governmental entity.

rules.legal_concept: Preservation hold on denied records during appeal
rules.atomic_rule: An entity may not destroy or give up custody of any record to which access was denied until the appeal period has expired or the appeals process (including judicial appeal) has ended.
rules.trigger: Access denied and appeal period/process pending
rules.source_language: Unless otherwise required by a court or agency of competent jurisdiction, a governmental entity may not destroy or give up custody of any record to which access was denied until the period for an appeal has expired or the end of the appeals process, including judicial appeal.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver #2: preservation hold triggered by the denial/appeal on this request.

rules.legal_concept: Mandatory denial of shared records with source referral
rules.atomic_rule: An entity may not provide a record it received as a shared record under § 63G-2-206; it must deny the request and inform the requester of the identity of the entity from which the shared record was received.
rules.trigger: Requested record was received as a shared record under § 63G-2-206
rules.source_language: (a) In response to a request for a record, a governmental entity may not provide a record that it has received under Section 63G-2-206 as a shared record. (b) If a governmental entity is prohibited from providing a record under Subsection (2)(a), the governmental entity shall: (i) deny the records request; and (ii) inform the person making the request of the identity of the governmental entity from which the shared record was received.
rules.notes: Routing: requester must be redirected to the originating entity.

rules.legal_concept: Classification deferred until access requested
rules.atomic_rule: An entity is not required to classify a particular record, record series, or information until access to the record is requested.
rules.trigger: Access to a record is requested
rules.source_language: A governmental entity may classify a particular record, record series, or information within a record at any time, but is not required to classify a particular record, record series, or information until access to the record is requested.
rules.notes: Drives when the classification step runs during request handling.

rules.legal_concept: Limited duty to respond to incarcerated/parolee requesters
rules.atomic_rule: An entity is not required to respond to a request by or on behalf of an individual on parole or confined in a correctional facility, except for the first five requests per calendar year seeking only records referencing that individual, or a request submitted by the individual's attorney.
rules.trigger: Requester is on parole or confined following conviction
rules.source_language: (a) Notwithstanding any other provision of this chapter, and subject to Subsection (9)(b), a governmental entity is not required to respond to, or provide a record in response to, a record request if the request is submitted by or in behalf of an individual who is on parole or confined in a jail or other correctional facility following the individual's conviction. (b) Subsection (9)(a) does not apply to: (i) the first five record requests submitted to the governmental entity by or in behalf of an individual described in Subsection (9)(a) during any calendar year requesting only a record that contains a specific reference to the individual; or (ii) a record request that is submitted by an attorney of an individual described in Subsection (9)(a).
rules.notes: Alters processing/routing for a requester class. Threshold: 5 requests/calendar year (floor of guaranteed responses).

rules.legal_concept: Vexatious requester relief
rules.atomic_rule: On a granted petition, the director may order that the entity is not required to fulfill requests from the respondent (or persons requesting on the respondent's behalf) for a period not exceeding one year.
rules.trigger: Director grants entity's vexatious-requester petition
rules.source_language: Upon granting the petition in whole or in part, the director may order that the governmental entity is not required to fulfill requests from the respondent or a person that submits a request on the respondent's behalf for a period of time that may not exceed one year.
rules.notes: Ceiling of one year. During the ordered period, § 63G-2-201(7)(a)(vi) relieves the entity of the duty to fulfill the requester's requests. Blocks the request at intake.

rules.legal_concept: Petition to declare a vexatious requester
rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity may file a petition with the director of the Government Records Office to obtain relief from a person it claims is a vexatious requester.
rules.trigger: Entity claims a person is a vexatious requester
rules.source_language: A governmental entity may file a petition with the director to request relief from a person that the governmental entity claims is a vexatious requester.
rules.notes: Structural branch: separate adjudicative process before the director (hearing scheduling parallels § 63G-2-403).

rules.legal_concept: No GRAMA appeal of requests blocked by vexatious order
rules.atomic_rule: A records request that an entity is not required to fulfill under a vexatious-requester order may not be the subject of a Part 4 appeal.
rules.trigger: Request falls under a vexatious-requester order
rules.source_language: Notwithstanding any other provision of this chapter, a records request that a governmental entity is not required to fulfill in accordance with an order issued under this section may not be the subject of an appeal under Part 4, Appeals.

rules.legal_concept: Appeal to chief administrative officer
rules.atomic_rule: A requester or interested party may appeal an access denial or fee-waiver denial to the chief administrative officer by filing a notice of appeal within 30 days after the denial notice is sent (or after a deemed denial under 204(9)).
rules.trigger: Access denial, deemed denial, or fee-waiver denial
rules.clock_spec: fixed: 30 calendar-days after notice of denial sent (or deemed denial under 204(9); or, for fee waiver, the date of the waiver-denial notice)
rules.source_language: A requester or interested party may appeal an access denial or the denial of a fee waiver under Subsection 63G-2-203(4) to the chief administrative officer of the governmental entity by filing a notice of appeal with the chief administrative officer within 30 days after: (i) for an access denial: (A) the governmental entity sends a notice of denial under Section 63G-2-205...; or (B) the record request is considered denied under Subsection 63G-2-204(9)...; or (ii) for a denial of a fee waiver, the date the governmental entity notifies the requester that the fee waiver is denied.
rules.notes: First-stage administrative appeal. Political subdivisions may set different appeal time limits under § 63G-2-701(4)(b).

rules.legal_concept: Appeal of extraordinary-circumstances claim/date
rules.atomic_rule: A requester who believes claimed extraordinary circumstances do not exist or the specified availability date is unreasonable may appeal to the chief administrative officer by filing a notice of appeal within 30 days after notification of the claim.
rules.trigger: Entity claims extraordinary circumstances and specifies an availability date
rules.clock_spec: fixed: 30 calendar-days after notification of the extraordinary-circumstances claim
rules.source_language: If a governmental entity claims extraordinary circumstances and specifies the date when the records will be available under Subsection 63G-2-204(4), and, if the requester believes the extraordinary circumstances do not exist or that the date specified is unreasonable, the requester may appeal the governmental entity's claim of extraordinary circumstances or date for compliance to the chief administrative officer by filing a notice of appeal with the chief administrative officer within 30 days after notification of a claim of extraordinary circumstances by the governmental entity...

rules.legal_concept: CAO decision deadline
rules.atomic_rule: The chief administrative officer must decide the appeal within 10 business days of receiving the notice of appeal (5 business days if expedited treatment benefits the public; 12 business days if a business-confidentiality claimant was noticed).
rules.trigger: CAO receives notice of appeal
rules.clock_spec: fixed: 10 business-days from receipt of notice of appeal (5 business-days if expedited benefits public; 12 business-days after notice sent to a business-confidentiality claimant)
rules.source_language: The chief administrative officer shall make a decision on the appeal within: (i)(A) 10 business days after the chief administrative officer's receipt of the notice of appeal; or (B) five business days after the chief administrative officer's receipt of the notice of appeal, if the requester or interested party demonstrates that an expedited decision benefits the public rather than the requester or interested party; or (ii) 12 business days after the governmental entity sends the notice of appeal to a person who submitted a claim of business confidentiality.
rules.notes: Parties may extend these periods by agreement (401(5)(c)).

rules.legal_concept: CAO non-decision deemed affirmance
rules.atomic_rule: If the chief administrative officer fails to decide within the specified time, the failure is the equivalent of a decision affirming the access denial (or affirming the extraordinary-circumstances claim/date, for a 401(1)(b) appeal).
rules.trigger: CAO does not decide within the deadline
rules.clock_spec: terminal at expiry of the CAO decision deadline (UT-0041)
rules.source_language: (i) If the chief administrative officer fails to make a decision on an appeal of an access denial within the time specified in Subsection (5)(a), the failure is the equivalent of a decision affirming the access denial. (ii) If the chief administrative officer fails to make a decision on an appeal under Subsection (1)(b) within the time specified in Subsection (5)(a), the failure is the equivalent of a decision affirming the claim of extraordinary circumstances or the reasonableness of the date specified when the records will be available.
rules.notes: Deemed-affirmance trigger; opens the next appeal stage (director / district court / local board).

rules.legal_concept: Contents of CAO decision notice affirming denial
rules.atomic_rule: A CAO decision affirming an access or fee-waiver denial must notify the requester of the right to ombudsman mediation, the right to appeal to the director/district court (or local appeals board), the appeal time limits and mediation suspension, and the names/addresses of the director, local board contact, and government records ombudsman.
rules.trigger: CAO affirms an access or fee-waiver denial
rules.source_language: If the chief administrative officer's decision is to affirm the access denial in whole or in part or to affirm the fee waiver denial, the notice under Subsection (7)(a) shall include: (i) a statement that the requester has a right under Section 63A-12-204 to request the government records ombudsman to mediate the dispute...; (ii) a statement that the requester or interested party has the right to appeal the decision, as provided in Section 63G-2-402, to: (A) the director or district court; or (B) the local appeals board, if the governmental entity is a political subdivision and the governmental entity has established a local appeals board; (iii) the time limits for filing an appeal..., including an explanation of a suspension of the time limits...for a requester if the requester seeks mediation under Section 63A-12-204; and (iv) the name and business address of: (A) the director; (B) the individual designated as the contact individual for the appeals board...; and (C) the government records ombudsman.

rules.legal_concept: Appeal to director of the Government Records Office
rules.atomic_rule: A records appellant appeals to the director by filing a notice of appeal no later than 30 days after the decision being appealed is issued (or, where the CAO fails to decide a 401(1)(b) matter, within 45 days after the record request is made).
rules.trigger: CAO (or local board) decision affirming denial issued, or CAO non-decision in an extraordinary-circumstances appeal
rules.clock_spec: fixed: 30 calendar-days after the appealed decision is issued (or 45 calendar-days after the record request is made in the 401(1)(b) non-decision case)
rules.source_language: (a) A records appellant appeals to the director by filing a notice of appeal with the director no later than 30 days after the day on which the decision being appealed is issued. (b) Notwithstanding Subsection (1)(a), a requester may file a notice of appeal with the director no later than 45 days after the day on which the record request is made if: (i) the circumstances described in Subsection 63G-2-401(1)(b) occur; and (ii) the chief administrative officer fails to make a decision under Section 63G-2-401.
rules.notes: Second-stage administrative appeal (state-level review body). Alternative to district court and, for political subdivisions with a board, to the local appeals board.

rules.legal_concept: Ombudsman mediation suspends appeal deadlines
rules.atomic_rule: The time for a requester to file a notice of appeal to the director (and a petition for judicial review) is suspended while government-records-ombudsman mediation is pending, ending when the ombudsman certifies the mediation concluded or did not occur.
rules.trigger: Requester submits a request for ombudsman mediation under § 63A-12-204
rules.clock_spec: tolls the 30/45-day director-appeal window and the 30-day judicial-review window from the mediation-request date until the ombudsman certifies conclusion/non-occurrence
rules.source_language: The time for a requester to file a notice of appeal under Subsection (1)(a) or (b) is suspended for the period of time that: (i) begins on the date the requester submits a request under Section 63A-12-204 for the government records ombudsman to mediate the dispute between the requester and the governmental entity; and (ii) ends the earlier of the following dates: (A) the date that the government records ombudsman certifies in writing that the mediation is concluded; or (B) the date that the government records ombudsman certifies in writing that the mediation did not occur or was not concluded because of a lack of the required consent.
rules.notes: Parallel tolling language appears in § 63G-2-404(1)(b) for the judicial-review deadline. Ombudsman mediation itself is governed by § 63A-12-204 (outside this chapter).

rules.legal_concept: Director hearing scheduling window
rules.atomic_rule: No later than 7 business days after receiving a notice of appeal, the director must schedule a hearing for the next regularly scheduled hearing date that is at least 16 but no later than 64 calendar days after the notice of appeal is filed.
rules.trigger: Director receives a notice of appeal
rules.clock_spec: fixed: schedule within 7 business-days of notice; hearing at least 16 and no later than 64 calendar-days after filing
rules.source_language: Except as provided in Subsections (4)(b) and (c), no later than seven business days after receiving a notice of appeal, the director shall: (i) schedule a hearing for the director to discuss the appeal at the next regularly scheduled hearing date that is at least 16 calendar days after the date the notice of appeal is filed but no later than 64 calendar days after the date the notice of appeal is filed, except that the director may schedule an expedited hearing upon application of the records appellant and good cause shown...
rules.notes: Director may schedule later than 64 days if that is the first hearing date with fewer than 10 appeals scheduled (403(4)(c)).

rules.legal_concept: Director decision deadline and deemed denial
rules.atomic_rule: The director must issue a signed order no later than 7 business days after the hearing; if the director fails to issue a decision within 73 calendar days after the notice of appeal is filed, that failure is deemed an order denying the appeal.
rules.trigger: Hearing held; or 73 calendar days elapse from filing without a decision
rules.clock_spec: fixed: order within 7 business-days after hearing; deemed denial at 73 calendar-days after notice of appeal filed
rules.source_language: No later than seven business days after the day of the hearing, the director shall issue a signed order: (i) granting the relief sought, in whole or in part; or (ii) upholding the governmental entity's access denial, in whole or in part. ... If the director fails to issue a decision within 73 calendar days after the day of the filing of the notice of appeal, that failure is the equivalent of an order denying the appeal.
rules.notes: Deemed-denial trigger at 73 calendar days; requester must notify the director in writing if treating the appeal as denied (403(13)(b)).

rules.legal_concept: Local appeals board (political subdivision)
rules.atomic_rule: A political subdivision may establish a three-member appeals board (one employee; two members of the public not employed by government, at least one with records experience) to decide appeals of a CAO decision; if established, CAO-decision appeals go to the board instead of the director.
rules.trigger: Political subdivision establishes a local appeals board
rules.source_language: (i) A political subdivision may establish an appeals board to decide an appeal of a decision of the chief administrative officer affirming an access denial. (ii) An appeals board established by a political subdivision shall be composed of three members: (A) one of whom shall be an employee of the political subdivision; and (B) two of whom shall be members of the public who are not employed by or officials of a governmental entity, at least one of whom shall have professional experience with requesting or managing records. (iii) If a political subdivision establishes an appeals board, any appeal of a decision of a chief administrative officer shall be made to the appeals board. (iv) If a political subdivision does not establish an appeals board, the political subdivision's appeals process shall provide for an appeal of a chief administrative officer's decision to the director of the Government Records Office...
rules.notes: Municipal-specific structural fork: the second-stage appeal path differs depending on whether the city has a local appeals board. A board decision is itself appealable to the director or district court (701(6)).

rules.legal_concept: Judicial review in district court
rules.atomic_rule: A petition for judicial review of an order or decision must be filed in district court no later than 30 days after the date of the order or decision.
rules.trigger: Appealable order or decision issued (director, local board, CAO, or vexatious-requester order)
rules.clock_spec: fixed: 30 calendar-days after the date of the order or decision (tolled during ombudsman mediation per UT-0058)
rules.source_language: A petition for judicial review of an order or decision, as allowed under this part, in Section 63G-2-209, or in Subsection 63G-2-701(6)(a)(ii), shall be filed no later than 30 days after the date of the order or decision, subject to Subsection (1)(b).
rules.notes: Judicial path (namespaced appeal.judicial). Court reviews de novo (404(6)(a)); may review disputed records in camera. A requester may go directly to district court from a CAO affirmance without first appealing to the director (§ 63G-2-402(1)(a)(ii)).

rules.legal_concept: Notice to business-confidentiality claimant on appeal
rules.atomic_rule: If an appeal involves a record subject to a business-confidentiality claim, the CAO must send notice of the appeal to the claimant within three business days of receiving notice, and the claimant then has seven business days to submit further support for the claim.
rules.trigger: Appeal involves a record with a § 63G-2-309 business-confidentiality claim
rules.clock_spec: CAO notice within 3 business-days of receiving the appeal; claimant has 7 business-days after notice to submit further support
rules.source_language: If the appeal involves a record that is the subject of a business confidentiality claim under Section 63G-2-309, the chief administrative officer shall: (i) send notice of the appeal to the business confidentiality claimant within three business days after receiving notice, except that if notice under this section must be given to more than 35 persons, it shall be given as soon as reasonably possible; and (ii) send notice of the business confidentiality claim and the schedule for the chief administrative officer's determination to the requester or interested party within three business days after receiving notice of the appeal. ... The business confidentiality claimant shall have seven business days after notice is sent by the administrative officer to submit further support for the claim of business confidentiality.
rules.notes: Third-party notice branch during the CAO appeal.

rules.legal_concept: Business confidentiality claim submission
rules.atomic_rule: A person who provides a record they believe should be protected as a trade secret/commercial information under 63G-2-305(1)/(2) must provide, with or within a reasonable time after the record, a written claim of business confidentiality and a concise statement of supporting reasons.
rules.trigger: Person submits a record believed protectable under § 63G-2-305(1) or (2)
rules.source_language: Any person who provides to a governmental entity a record that the person believes should be protected under Subsection 63G-2-305(1) or (2) or both Subsections 63G-2-305(1) and (2) shall provide with the record, or within a reasonable amount of time after providing the record: (A) a written claim of business confidentiality; and (B) a concise statement of reasons supporting the claim of business confidentiality.
rules.notes: Creates a distinct redaction/notice workflow; the claim triggers appeal-notice duties (UT-0062) and a disclosure hold (UT-0064).

rules.legal_concept: Hold on disclosing claimed-confidential records pending appeal
rules.atomic_rule: An entity that determines a record claimed as business-confidential should nonetheless be disclosed may not disclose it until the appeal period expires or the appeals process (including judicial appeal) ends, unless the claimant waived the claim by not appealing/intervening.
rules.trigger: Entity decides to release a record over a pending business-confidentiality claim
rules.source_language: Except as provided in Subsection (2)(b) or by court order, the governmental entity to whom the request for a record is made may not disclose a record claimed to be protected under a provision listed in Subsection (1)(b)(i) but which the governmental entity or the director of the Government Records Office determines should be disclosed until the period in which to bring an appeal expires or the end of the appeals process, including judicial appeal.
rules.notes: Disclosure hold parallel to the denied-record hold (UT-0046).

rules.legal_concept: Production and notice of compliance after director order
rules.atomic_rule: If the director orders production and no appeal is filed (or production is required as a result of appeal), the governmental entity must produce the record and file a notice of compliance with the director.
rules.trigger: Director orders production and no notice of intent to appeal is filed
