rules.source_language: If the director orders the governmental entity to produce a record and no appeal is filed, or if, as a result of the appeal, the governmental entity is required to produce a record, the governmental entity shall: (i) produce the record; and (ii) file a notice of compliance with the director.
rules.notes: Post-order production step. Failure to comply or appeal can draw a civil penalty of up to $500/day (403(15)(d)) — remedy amount excluded per inclusion test.

rules.legal_concept: Political subdivisions may set different response/appeal timeframes
rules.atomic_rule: In its records ordinance/policy, a political subdivision may establish reasonable response times and appeal time limits different from those in § 63G-2-204 and Part 4 if it determines its resources are insufficient to meet those sections.
rules.trigger: Political subdivision adopts a records ordinance/policy and finds insufficient resources
rules.source_language: (a) Each ordinance or policy shall establish access criteria, procedures, and response times for requests to inspect, obtain, or amend records of the political subdivision, and time limits for appeals consistent with this chapter. (b) In establishing response times for access requests and time limits for appeals, the political subdivision may establish reasonable time frames different than those set out in Section 63G-2-204 and Part 4, Appeals, if it determines that the resources of the political subdivision are insufficient to meet the requirements of those sections.
rules.notes: Critical municipal-config fork: a city's actual response/appeal deadlines may differ from the statutory defaults (UT-0009, UT-0010, UT-0040, UT-0041, UT-0056). A political subdivision that adopts no ordinance/policy is fully subject to this chapter (701(2)(c)); regardless of any ordinance it remains subject to Parts 1 & 3 and §§ 201, 202, 205, 206, 601, 602 (701(2)(d)).

structural_branches.description: Request enters an extended-processing state on an extraordinary-circumstances claim (UT-0014/0015), with ground-specific extension deadlines (UT-0016 5-day legal review; UT-0017 15-day editing; UT-0018 soft ASAP for volume/programming).
Prepayment gate (UT-0037/0038): the request is held before processing when estimated fees exceed $50 or prior fees are unpaid.

Municipal fork (UT-0057): a political subdivision may create a 3-member local appeals board; if it does, the second-stage appeal of a CAO decision goes to that board rather than to the director of the Government Records Office.

State-level second-stage appeal to the director of the Government Records Office (UT-0056/0059/0060), a distinct adjudicative body with its own hearing scheduling (16-64 day) and a 73-calendar-day deemed-denial backstop.

Ombudsman-mediation branch (UT-0058): submitting a § 63A-12-204 mediation request tolls both the director-appeal and judicial-review filing windows until the ombudsman certifies conclusion or non-occurrence.

Vexatious-requester adjudication before the director (UT-0051/0052/0053): an entity can petition to be relieved (up to one year) of the duty to fulfill a person's requests; such blocked requests are not appealable under Part 4.
Business-confidentiality workflow (UT-0062/0063/0064): a submitter's trade-secret claim triggers claimant notice on appeal (3-day / 7-day) and a disclosure hold pending appeal.

Municipal timeframe fork (UT-0049): a city's ordinance may set response and appeal deadlines different from the statutory defaults where resources are insufficient — the operative per-request deadlines can be city-specific.
Deemed-denial state transition (UT-0019): silence past the response window becomes an appealable denial. Parallel deemed outcomes exist at the CAO stage (UT-0042) and director stage (UT-0060).

material_negatives.note: GRAMA sets no separate acknowledgment/receipt-confirmation deadline distinct from the substantive 10/5-business-day response window in § 63G-2-204(4). No found rule requiring an interim acknowledgment.

No explicit clarification clock or nonresponse-abandonment/withdrawal procedure found. A request must be reasonably specific (§ 63G-2-204(1)(a)(ii)) but GRAMA does not codify a tolling clarification exchange or deem an unclarified request abandoned. Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

Chapter 2 contains no codified Saturday/Sunday/holiday day-counting rule. Guidance (Utah State Archives / ombudsman) states business days exclude weekends and legal holidays and that periods over 11 days are counted as calendar days, but this was not located in the statute itself this pass — flagged for an administrative-rule / guidance pass.

No statewide per-page copy rate. Fees are actual-cost-based (§ 63G-2-203) and set by each political subdivision by ordinance/policy (§ 63G-2-203(3)(c)); the per-page value is a city-supplied parameter, not a state number.
No fixed deposit percentage; prepayment is of past plus estimated future fees in full, gated by the $50 threshold (§ 63G-2-203(8)). No partial-deposit formula found.

Related caveat: GRAMA has no explicit anti-purpose-discrimination clause in current § 63G-2-201; the no-purpose fact (UT-0003) is inferred from the request-content list. An older/handbook statement that access cannot be restricted based on the reason for the request should be verified against statute/case law in a later pass.

rules.legal_concept: Right of residents and all other interested persons to examine public records
rules.atomic_rule: Any resident of the state and any other person interested in examining public records is empowered to examine those records and make memoranda, copies, and abstracts, free of charge, during office business hours.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional right, subject to statutory exceptions).
rules.source_language: all residents of this state and all other persons interested in the examination of the public records ... are hereby fully empowered and authorized to (a) examine such records, and make memoranda, copies ... all free of charge, during the hours the respective offices may be kept open for the ordinary transaction of business
rules.effective_status: Current (amended 2024 Neb. Laws LB 43, operative July 19, 2024)
rules.notes: Universal-access symmetry: emitted as a rule with the shared eligibility key. Ellipses reflect the operative clause as captured from the opened statute; full-text spot-check recommended.

rules.legal_concept: Access extends beyond residents to all other interested persons
rules.atomic_rule: Eligibility to examine and copy public records is not limited to residents; 'all other persons interested in the examination of the public records' are equally authorized, so no residency or citizenship qualification gates the right.
rules.trigger: None stated.
rules.source_language: all residents of this state and all other persons interested in the examination of the public records ... are hereby fully empowered and authorized to (a) examine such records
rules.notes: 2024 LB 43 broadened the class from 'citizens' to 'residents' while retaining 'all other persons,' so no residency requirement bars access. Emitted as a rule with the shared key per universal-access symmetry.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required to examine records
rules.atomic_rule: A requester need not state a reason or purpose to examine or obtain public records; the right to examine attaches to any interested person without a purpose condition.
rules.trigger: None stated.
rules.source_language: all residents of this state and all other persons interested in the examination of the public records ... are hereby fully empowered and authorized to (a) examine such records, and make memoranda, copies
rules.notes: Emitted as a rule with the shared key per universal-access symmetry. The 'no purpose' conclusion is derived from the absence of any purpose condition in the empowerment clause; commercial purpose is relevant only to the discretionary fee waiver (NE-0022), not to the right of access.

rules.legal_concept: Records presumed public unless another statute expressly makes them confidential; liberal construction
rules.atomic_rule: All records and documents, regardless of physical form, are public records except when another statute expressly provides they shall not be made public; the public-records sections are liberally construed toward full access.
rules.trigger: None stated.
rules.source_language: Except when any other statute expressly provides that particular information or records shall not be made public, public records shall include all records and documents, regardless of physical form ... Sections 84-712 to 84-712.03 shall be liberally construed ... in order that the residents of this state shall have the full right to know of and have full access to information on the public finances of the government
rules.notes: Drives the default-open branch: the engine treats a record as disclosable unless an express statutory exception is invoked.

rules.legal_concept: Definition of public records regardless of physical form
rules.atomic_rule: Public records include all records and documents, regardless of physical form, of or belonging to the state or any county, city, village, political subdivision, tax-supported district, or their agencies/boards/subunits.
rules.trigger: None stated.
rules.source_language: public records shall include all records and documents, regardless of physical form, of or belonging to this state, any county, city, village, political subdivision, or tax-supported district in this state, or any agency, branch, department, board, bureau, commission, council, subunit, or committee of any of the foregoing.
rules.notes: The software branches on whether the requested item is a covered public record.

rules.legal_concept: Cities, villages, and political subdivisions are covered public bodies
rules.atomic_rule: Records of or belonging to any city, village, political subdivision, or tax-supported district are public records subject to the Act, bringing municipal bodies within its coverage.
rules.trigger: Custodian is a city, village, or other local subdivision.
rules.source_language: public records shall include all records and documents, regardless of physical form, of or belonging to this state, any county, city, village, political subdivision, or tax-supported district in this state
rules.notes: Confirms the Act reaches the municipal custodians this build targets.

rules.legal_concept: Requester may examine and make own copies free of charge
rules.atomic_rule: A requester may examine records and make memoranda, copies (using their own copying/photocopying equipment on the custodian's premises), and abstracts, all free of charge.
rules.trigger: Examination occurs on the custodian's premises during business hours.
rules.source_language: (a) examine such records, and make memoranda, copies ... all free of charge, during the hours the respective offices may be kept open for the ordinary transaction of business
rules.notes: On-premises self-copying with own equipment is free; a custodian-produced copy triggers the fee/estimate process (NE-0011, NE-0019).

rules.legal_concept: Access during ordinary office business hours
rules.atomic_rule: Examination and copying rights are exercisable during the hours the respective offices are kept open for the ordinary transaction of business.
rules.trigger: Request to examine on premises.
rules.source_language: during the hours the respective offices may be kept open for the ordinary transaction of business
rules.notes: State sets the standard ('office business hours'); the individual municipality supplies the actual hours value.

rules.legal_concept: No fee for examination or self-made copies
rules.atomic_rule: No fee may be charged for examining records or for memoranda/copies/abstracts the requester makes with their own equipment; these are free of charge.
rules.trigger: Examination or self-copying (as opposed to custodian-produced copies).
rules.source_language: examine such records, and make memoranda, copies ... all free of charge
rules.notes: Free-allowance value is fixed at $0 for inspection/self-copy; distinct from the actual-added-cost ceiling on custodian-produced copies (NE-0019).

rules.legal_concept: Written request triggers the copy/estimate and response duty
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian's duty to provide a cost estimate and one of the enumerated responses is triggered by receipt of a written request for access to or copies of a public record.
rules.trigger: Custodian receives a written request for access or copies.
rules.source_language: Upon receiving a written request for access to or copies of a public record, the custodian of such record shall provide to the requester as soon as is practicable and without delay, but not more than four business days after actual receipt of the request
rules.notes: On-premises examination requires no written request; the formal response clock attaches to a written request.

rules.legal_concept: Four-business-day response deadline
rules.atomic_rule: Within not more than four business days after actual receipt of a written request, the custodian must provide a cost estimate and either (a) access/copies, (b) a written denial, or (c) a written explanation of delay.
rules.trigger: Actual receipt of a written request.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 4 business-days from actual receipt of the written request
rules.source_language: the custodian of such record shall provide to the requester as soon as is practicable and without delay, but not more than four business days after actual receipt of the request, an estimate of the expected cost of the copies and either (a) access to or, if copying equipment is reasonably available, copies of the public record, (b) if there is a legal basis for denial of access or copies, a written denial of the request ... or (c) if the entire request cannot with reasonable good faith efforts be fulfilled within four business days after actual receipt of the request due to the significant difficulty or the extensiveness of the request, a written explanation
rules.notes: 'Not more than four business days' is a ceiling on the response time; the soft 'as soon as is practicable and without delay' standard runs concurrently (NE-0012).

rules.legal_concept: Response as soon as practicable and without delay
rules.atomic_rule: Independent of the four-day cap, the custodian must respond as soon as is practicable and without delay.
rules.trigger: Actual receipt of a written request.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "as soon as is practicable and without delay" from actual receipt
rules.source_language: as soon as is practicable and without delay, but not more than four business days after actual receipt of the request
rules.notes: Soft standard preserved as source term; the engine applies it as a promptness duty layered under the four-day ceiling, not a fillable value.

rules.legal_concept: Initial response must take one of three enumerated forms
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian's timely response must be one of three enumerated forms: (a) access/copies, (b) a written denial with a legal basis, or (c) a written explanation of delay.
rules.trigger: Custodian responding to a written request.
rules.source_language: either (a) access to or, if copying equipment is reasonably available, copies of the public record, (b) if there is a legal basis for denial of access or copies, a written denial of the request ... or (c) ... a written explanation
rules.notes: Structural fork: engine must be able to route a request to grant, denial, or delay-explanation.

rules.legal_concept: Written explanation of delay with earliest practicable date
rules.atomic_rule: When a request cannot with reasonable good-faith efforts be fulfilled within four business days due to significant difficulty or extensiveness, the custodian must give a written explanation including the earliest practicable date for fulfilling the request, a cost estimate, and an opportunity for the requester to modify or prioritize items.
rules.trigger: Request cannot be fulfilled within four business days due to significant difficulty or extensiveness.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "earliest practicable date for fulfilling the request" stated in the written explanation
rules.source_language: if the entire request cannot with reasonable good faith efforts be fulfilled within four business days after actual receipt of the request due to the significant difficulty or the extensiveness of the request, a written explanation, including the earliest practicable date for fulfilling the request, an estimate of the expected cost of any copies, and an opportunity for the requester to modify or prioritize the items
rules.notes: Nebraska-specific delay path; the 'earliest practicable date' is a soft-standard deadline the engine tracks, not a numeric window.

rules.legal_concept: Requester's ten-business-day window to review costs and act
rules.atomic_rule: After receiving the cost estimate, the requester has ten business days to review estimated costs (including any special service charge) and either request fulfillment of the original request, negotiate to narrow/simplify it, or withdraw it.
rules.trigger: Custodian provides an estimate of expected costs.
rules.clock_spec: 10 business-days from delivery of the cost estimate
rules.source_language: The requester shall have ten business days to review the estimated costs, including any special service charge, and request the custodian to fulfill the original request, negotiate with the custodian to narrow or simplify the request, or withdraw the request.
rules.notes: Added by the 2024 amendment; creates a requester-action window that gates whether the custodian proceeds.

rules.legal_concept: Custodian may not proceed if requester does not respond in ten business days
rules.atomic_rule: If the requester does not respond to the custodian within ten business days of the cost estimate, the custodian shall not proceed to fulfill the request.
rules.trigger: Requester fails to respond within ten business days of the estimate.
rules.clock_spec: terminal at 10 business-days from cost estimate; nonresponse halts fulfillment
rules.source_language: If the requester does not respond to the custodian within ten business days, the custodian shall not proceed to fulfill the request.
rules.notes: Constructive abandonment: silence after the estimate ends the custodian's obligation to fulfill.

rules.legal_concept: Computation of business days and definition of business day
rules.atomic_rule: The four business days are computed by excluding the day the request is received; a business day excludes Saturdays, Sundays, and any day the custodian's offices are closed.
rules.trigger: Computing a statutory deadline.
rules.source_language: The four business days shall be computed by excluding the day the request is received, after which the designated period of time begins to run. Business day does not include a Saturday, a Sunday, or a day during which the offices of the custodian of the public records are closed.
rules.notes: Calculation rule the engine executes to compute the four-business-day deadline (and, by definition of business day, the ten-business-day window).

rules.legal_concept: Custodian must provide a cost estimate
rules.atomic_rule: With its timely response, the custodian must provide the requester an estimate of the expected cost of the copies.
rules.trigger: Written request for copies received.
rules.source_language: the custodian of such record shall provide to the requester ... an estimate of the expected cost of the copies
rules.notes: The estimate starts the requester's ten-business-day review window (NE-0015).

rules.legal_concept: Copy fee capped at actual added cost
rules.atomic_rule: A custodian may charge a fee for providing copies, but the fee shall not exceed the actual added cost of making the copies available.
rules.trigger: Custodian produces copies for the requester.
rules.source_language: the public body, public entity, or public official which is the custodian of a public record may charge a fee for providing copies of such public record ... which fee shall not exceed the actual added cost
rules.effective_status: Current (fee limits tightened by 2024 Neb. Laws LB 43)
rules.notes: Ceiling of 'actual added cost'; no statewide per-page cents rate — the municipality supplies the operative rate under the ceiling.

rules.legal_concept: First eight cumulative hours of labor not chargeable to residents
rules.atomic_rule: For a Nebraska resident's request, the actual added cost used to calculate a fee shall not include any charge for existing salary/pay obligations for the first eight cumulative hours of searching, identifying, physically redacting, or copying.
rules.trigger: Requester is a resident; labor total is within the first eight cumulative hours.
rules.source_language: the actual added cost used as the basis for the calculation of a fee for records shall not include any charge for the existing salary or pay obligation to the public officers or employees with respect to the first eight cumulative hours of searching, identifying, physically redacting, or copying
rules.notes: Fixed free-labor allowance of eight cumulative hours for residents; labor beyond eight hours may be recovered as a special service charge (referenced in the cost-review clause, NE-0015).

rules.legal_concept: Deposit may be required when estimated cost exceeds fifty dollars
rules.atomic_rule: If the estimated cost of requested copies exceeds fifty dollars, the custodian may require the requester to furnish a deposit before fulfilling the request.
rules.trigger: Estimated cost of copies exceeds $50.
rules.source_language: If copies requested ... are estimated by the custodian of such public records to cost more than fifty dollars, the custodian may require the requester to furnish a deposit prior to fulfilling such request.
rules.notes: The $50 trigger threshold is fixed by statute; the deposit amount itself is discretionary within the actual-cost ceiling.

rules.legal_concept: Discretionary fee waiver or reduction in the public interest
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian may waive or reduce any fee if the waiver or reduction would be in the public interest.
rules.trigger: Custodian determines waiver/reduction is in the public interest.
rules.source_language: The custodian may waive or reduce any fee described in this section if the waiver or reduction of the fee would be in the public interest.
rules.notes: Discretionary; no numeric standard, so config_home is structural.

rules.legal_concept: Reasonable fee for modem/electronic transmission of county records
rules.atomic_rule: When a county custodian provides a copy by transmitting it modem-to-modem, a reasonable fee may be charged for the specialized service, which may include a reasonable amortization of added computer equipment/software cost.
rules.trigger: Record delivered by modem-to-modem transmission by a county custodian.
rules.source_language: When a custodian of a public record of a county provides to a member of the public, upon request, a copy of the public record by transmitting it from a modem to an outside modem, a reasonable fee may be charged for such specialized service. Such fee may include a reasonable amount representing a portion of the amortization of the cost of computer equipment, including software, necessarily added in order to provide such specialized service.
rules.notes: 'Reasonable fee' is a soft-standard value; text is county-specific.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to acquire new computer capability to generate records in a new form
rules.atomic_rule: A governmental entity is not required to acquire computer capability to generate public records in a new or different form when that new form would require additional computer equipment or software the entity does not already possess.
rules.trigger: Request would require generating records in a new/different form needing equipment/software not already held.
rules.source_language: This subsection shall not be construed to require a governmental entity to acquire computer capability to generate public records in a new or different form when that new form would require additional computer equipment or software not already possessed by the governmental entity.
rules.notes: Limits format/creation obligations; engine can gate requests that would require new-form generation.

rules.legal_concept: Data in computer files remains a public record
rules.atomic_rule: Data that is a public record in its original form remains a public record when maintained in computer files.
rules.trigger: Requested data is maintained in computer files.
rules.source_language: Data which is a public record in its original form shall remain a public record when maintained in computer files.
rules.notes: Electronic form does not defeat public-record status.

rules.legal_concept: Denial must be in writing where a legal basis exists
rules.atomic_rule: If there is a legal basis for denial, the custodian must issue a written denial of the request.
rules.trigger: Custodian withholds access/copies on a legal basis.
rules.source_language: if there is a legal basis for denial of access or copies, a written denial of the request together with the information specified in section 84-712.04
rules.notes: Parent denial rule; the required contents are split into NE-0027 through NE-0029 and linked.

rules.legal_concept: Denial must describe withheld records and cite specific statutory exception, correlating portions to reasons
rules.atomic_rule: A denial must include a description of the contents of the records withheld and a statement of specific reasons, correlating specific portions of the records to specific reasons, including citations to the particular statute and subsection expressly providing the exception.
rules.trigger: Custodian issues a written denial.
rules.source_language: A description of the contents of the records withheld and a statement of the specific reasons for the denial, correlating specific portions of the records to specific reasons for the denial, including citations to the particular statute and subsection thereof expressly providing the exception
rules.notes: Portion-by-portion correlation implies a segregability/partial-redaction analysis at the denial stage.

rules.legal_concept: Denial must name the responsible official or employee
rules.atomic_rule: A denial must state the name of the public official or employee responsible for the decision to deny the request.
rules.trigger: Custodian issues a written denial.
rules.source_language: The name of the public official or employee responsible for the decision to deny the request.

rules.legal_concept: Denial must notify of administrative/judicial review rights
rules.atomic_rule: A denial must notify the requester of any administrative or judicial right of review under section 84-712.03.
rules.trigger: Custodian issues a written denial.
rules.source_language: Notification to the requester of any administrative or judicial right of review under section 84-712.03.

rules.legal_concept: Public body must keep a publicly accessible file of denial letters
rules.atomic_rule: Each public body must maintain a file of all letters denying requests, and that file must be made accessible to the public upon request.
rules.trigger: A denial letter is issued.
rules.source_language: Each public body shall maintain a file of all letters of denial of requests for records; such file shall be made accessible to any member of the public upon request.
rules.effective_status: Current — Requires manual verification of exact text
rules.notes: is_paraphrase=true: captured from an opened-source summary, not confirmed verbatim; verify the exact clause. Kept as a rule because it is a document/log step tied to denial processing.

rules.legal_concept: Public body bears the burden to sustain withholding
rules.atomic_rule: In an enforcement action the burden is on the public body to sustain its action in withholding records.
rules.trigger: Judicial review of a withholding.
rules.source_language: The burden is on the public body to sustain its action.
rules.notes: Excerpted from § 84-712.03(2); full subsection also grants the court jurisdiction to enjoin withholding and order disclosure.

rules.legal_concept: Writ of mandamus in district court for denied access
rules.atomic_rule: A person denied access may file for speedy relief by a writ of mandamus in the district court within whose jurisdiction the custodian may be served.
rules.trigger: Denial of access to public records.
rules.source_language: File for speedy relief by a writ of mandamus in the district court within whose jurisdiction the ... custodian ... may be served
rules.notes: Judicial enforcement path (namespaced judicial). Clause excerpted from opened source; verify full text.

rules.legal_concept: Petition the Attorney General to review a denial
rules.atomic_rule: A person denied access may petition the Attorney General to review whether the record may be withheld or whether the public body failed to comply.
rules.trigger: Denial of access to public records.
rules.source_language: Petition the Attorney General to review the matter ... to determine whether the record may be withheld from public inspection
rules.notes: Administrative-style review by the AG (namespaced administrative). Alternative to mandamus. Clause excerpted; verify full text.

rules.legal_concept: Attorney General must decide petition within fifteen calendar days
rules.atomic_rule: The Attorney General must make a determination on the petition within fifteen calendar days after the submission of the petition.
rules.trigger: Petition to the Attorney General submitted.
rules.clock_spec: 15 calendar-days from submission of the petition
rules.source_language: within fifteen calendar days after the submission of the petition
rules.notes: Fixed statutory window. Excerpted from opened source.

rules.legal_concept: AG must bring suit within fifteen days of written demand after finding noncompliance
rules.atomic_rule: If the public body continues to refuse after the Attorney General finds noncompliance, the requester may sue directly or demand in writing that the Attorney General bring suit; the Attorney General must then bring suit within fifteen calendar days after receipt of the demand.
rules.trigger: Continued refusal after AG determination of noncompliance and a written demand to the AG.
rules.clock_spec: 15 calendar-days from AG receipt of the written demand to sue
rules.source_language: demand in writing that the Attorney General bring suit ... [the Attorney General shall] bring suit within fifteen calendar days after its receipt
rules.notes: Excerpted from two operative fragments in the opened source; verify continuous full text.

rules.legal_concept: Public-records suits advanced and given docket precedence
rules.atomic_rule: Proceedings to enforce public-records rights must be advanced on the trial docket and take precedence over all other cases.
rules.trigger: Public-records enforcement action filed.
rules.source_language: advanced on the trial docket and ... take precedence on the trial docket over all other cases
rules.notes: Expedited-docket procedural path. Clause excerpted from opened source; no numeric limitation period stated, so config_home is structural.

structural_branches.description: The initial response forks into three engine-executable paths: grant access/copies, written denial, or written explanation of delay (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 84-712(4)) — NE-0013.

Option (c) delay path: written explanation with earliest-practicable-date, cost estimate, and requester modify/prioritize opportunity when the request is significantly difficult or extensive — NE-0014.
Post-estimate requester-action stage (10 business days) to fulfill, negotiate, or withdraw, added by 2024 LB 43 — NE-0015; nonresponse halts fulfillment (NE-0016).
Attorney General review path as an alternative to court: petition → AG determination in 15 calendar days → possible AG-brought enforcement suit — NE-0033/0034/0035.
Mandamus enforcement path in district court with docket precedence and burden on the public body — NE-0032/0031/0036.
Denial-letter file each public body must maintain and expose to the public on request — NE-0030.

material_negatives.note: No express statute deeming custodian silence a denial. Nebraska instead imposes an affirmative four-business-day duty (§ 84-712(4)) plus remedies for 'denial' (§ 84-712.03); a failure to respond is treated as reviewable noncompliance rather than a statutorily 'deemed denial.' Absence of a found deemed-denial trigger is not proof none exists.

No standalone 'reasonably segregable — release the rest' production mandate located as a discrete clause. Partial coverage exists: § 84-712.04(1) requires denials to correlate specific withheld portions to specific reasons, and § 84-712(1) references 'physically redacting,' both implying portion-level redaction. Verify whether a freestanding segregability duty exists.

No statutory requirement that a public body designate/publicly identify a records or FOIA officer. Duties run to the 'lawful custodian' (whoever holds custody); no designation-and-publication step was found.
No express provision requiring retention/preservation of a requested record while the request or an appeal is pending. Routine retention schedules are governed separately and excluded.
No statewide fixed per-page copy rate. Copy fees are capped only at 'actual added cost' (§ 84-712(1), NE-0019); the municipality supplies the operative rate under that ceiling.

No separate custodian-initiated clarification clock. The nearest mechanism is the post-estimate 10-business-day requester window to negotiate/narrow (§ 84-712(4), NE-0015), which is requester-driven rather than a custodian clarification demand.
No acknowledgment step distinct from the substantive four-business-day response; the single four-day duty (NE-0011) subsumes acknowledgment.

EXCLUDED (inclusion test / Remove list — criminal penalties): § 84-712.09 makes a violating official subject to removal or impeachment and guilty of a Class III misdemeanor. Nothing in per-request software processing changes; recorded as audit trail, not a rule.

EXCLUDED (Remove list — attorney-fee provisions): § 84-712.07 authorizes equitable relief and reasonable attorney fees/litigation costs to a substantially prevailing complainant. Remedy amount, not a request-processing step.

EXCLUDED (exemptions not inventoried): § 84-712.05 lists ~30 discretionary categories a lawful custodian 'may withhold.' Only the general discretionary-withholding posture is captured via classification.presumption_of_openness (NE-0004) and the denial-specificity rules; the individual confidentiality categories do not each create a distinct processing workflow and are not enumerated as rows.

rules.legal_concept: Right of any person to inspect or copy public records
rules.atomic_rule: Any person (individual, corporation, partnership, firm, organization, or association) has a right to inspect, copy, or receive an electronic transmission of any public record of a public body, subject to exemptions and reasonable time/place rules.
rules.trigger: None stated (universal right)
rules.source_language: (A)(1) A person has a right to inspect, copy, or receive an electronic transmission of any public record of a public body, except as otherwise provided by Section 30-4-40, or other state and federal laws, in accordance with reasonable rules concerning time and place of access.
rules.notes: Standing to make a request runs to any "person" (§ 30-4-20(b) defines person broadly); no citizenship required to request records. Note: standing to bring the § 30-4-100 enforcement suit is limited to a "citizen of the State" — see SC-0035.

rules.legal_concept: No residency or citizenship requirement to request records
rules.atomic_rule: There is no residency or state-citizenship requirement to request records; the right runs to any "person" without qualification as to residence.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: (A)(1) A person has a right to inspect, copy, or receive an electronic transmission of any public record of a public body, except as otherwise provided by Section 30-4-40, or other state and federal laws, in accordance with reasonable rules concerning time and place of access.
rules.notes: Emitted as an affirmative universal-access rule per contract. The statute grants the right to "a person" with no residency limitation; absence of a residency requirement is inferred from the operative grant, not from a clause expressly disclaiming residency.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required
rules.atomic_rule: A requester need not state a reason or purpose for the request; the statutory right to inspect/copy is unconditioned on purpose.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: (A)(1) A person has a right to inspect, copy, or receive an electronic transmission of any public record of a public body, except as otherwise provided by Section 30-4-40, or other state and federal laws, in accordance with reasonable rules concerning time and place of access.
rules.notes: Emitted as an affirmative universal-access rule per contract. The statute imposes no purpose/use condition on the right to inspect or copy (a fee-waiver public-interest inquiry exists at SC-0015, but no purpose statement is required to obtain records).

rules.legal_concept: Incarcerated persons excluded from FOIA right
rules.atomic_rule: The right to inspect/copy does not extend to individuals serving a sentence of imprisonment in a state, county, or federal correctional facility (whether in South Carolina or elsewhere); their constitutionally protected rights, including the right to call for evidence in a criminal prosecution, are preserved.
rules.trigger: Requester is serving a sentence of imprisonment
rules.source_language: This right does not extend to individuals serving a sentence of imprisonment in a state or county correctional facility in this State, in another state, or in a federal correctional facility; however, this may not be construed to prevent those individuals from exercising their constitutionally protected rights, including, but not limited to, their right to call for evidence in their favor in a criminal prosecution under the South Carolina Rules of Criminal Procedure.
rules.notes: Requester-class exclusion that routes/blocks handling — a branch the engine must execute. Preserves constitutional discovery rights, so the exclusion is not absolute as to criminal-prosecution evidence.

rules.legal_concept: Written request triggers statutory response duties
rules.atomic_rule: The statutory determination/response duties and their clocks are triggered by a written request for records made under the chapter.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a written request for records
rules.source_language: Each public body, upon written request for records made under this chapter, shall within ten days (excepting Saturdays, Sundays, and legal public holidays) of the receipt of the request, notify the person making the request of its determination and the reasons for it
rules.notes: The determination/response obligation attaches to a "written request." Certain enumerated records are available in person without a written request (SC-0033). No statutory prescribed form/portal is mandated.

rules.legal_concept: Access subject to reasonable rules on time and place
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may condition access on reasonable rules concerning the time and place of access.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: A person has a right to inspect, copy, or receive an electronic transmission of any public record of a public body, except as otherwise provided by Section 30-4-40, or other state and federal laws, in accordance with reasonable rules concerning time and place of access.
rules.notes: "Reasonable" is an undefined standard — kept as source term, not converted to a value.

rules.legal_concept: Fees limited to actual cost of search, retrieval, and redaction
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may establish and collect reasonable fees not to exceed the actual cost of the search, retrieval, and redaction of records.
rules.trigger: Records request requiring search/retrieval/redaction
rules.source_language: The public body may establish and collect fees as provided for in this section. The public body may establish and collect reasonable fees not to exceed the actual cost of the search, retrieval, and redaction of records.
rules.effective_status: Current (2017 Act No. 67 revised fee structure)
rules.notes: Ceiling = actual cost; city sets the operative fee under it. Note redaction time IS chargeable here, but exemption-review time is NOT (SC-0013) — the two are distinguished.

rules.legal_concept: Search/retrieval/redaction labor rate capped at lowest-paid-qualified-employee salary
rules.atomic_rule: The fee for search, retrieval, or redaction shall not exceed the prorated hourly salary of the lowest paid employee who, in the custodian's reasonable discretion, has the necessary skill and training to perform the request.
rules.trigger: Charging a search/retrieval/redaction labor fee
rules.source_language: The fee for the search, retrieval, or redaction of records shall not exceed the prorated hourly salary of the lowest paid employee who, in the reasonable discretion of the custodian of the records, has the necessary skill and training to perform the request.
rules.notes: Ceiling tied to a computed value (prorated hourly salary of lowest-paid qualified employee); city supplies the actual rate under the cap.

rules.legal_concept: Copy fee capped at prevailing commercial rate
rules.atomic_rule: Fees for copies may not exceed the prevailing commercial rate for the producing of copies.
rules.trigger: Charging for copies of records
rules.source_language: Fees charged by a public body must be uniform for copies of the same record or document and may not exceed the prevailing commercial rate for the producing of copies.
rules.notes: Ceiling = prevailing commercial rate; no fixed per-page cents figure is set by statute (see material negatives).

rules.legal_concept: Copy fees must be uniform for the same record
rules.atomic_rule: Fees charged must be uniform for copies of the same record or document across requesters.
rules.trigger: Charging for copies of records
rules.source_language: Fees charged by a public body must be uniform for copies of the same record or document and may not exceed the prevailing commercial rate for the producing of copies.
rules.notes: Split from SC-0009: a non-discrimination standard (uniformity) distinct from the commercial-rate ceiling, drawn from the same sentence.

rules.legal_concept: No copy charge for records transmitted electronically
rules.atomic_rule: Copy charges may not be applied to records that are transmitted in an electronic format.
rules.trigger: Record is transmitted in electronic format
rules.source_language: Copy charges may not apply to records that are transmitted in an electronic format.
rules.notes: Fixed value of $0 for the copy-charge component when delivery is electronic. Search/retrieval/redaction labor may still be charged; only the per-copy charge is barred.

rules.legal_concept: Charge permitted for converting non-electronic records to electronic format
rules.atomic_rule: If records are not in electronic format and the public body agrees to produce them electronically, it may charge for the staff time required to transfer the documents to electronic format.
rules.trigger: Records not in electronic format and public body agrees to produce electronically
rules.source_language: If records are not in electronic format and the public body agrees to produce them in electronic format, the public body may charge for the staff time required to transfer the documents to electronic format.
rules.notes: Chargeable amount is "staff time," bounded by the labor-rate cap (SC-0008); no separate rate is fixed. Conversion charge is an exception to the no-electronic-copy-charge rule (SC-0011).

rules.legal_concept: No fee for examination/review to determine disclosability
rules.atomic_rule: Fees may not be charged for examination and review to determine if documents are subject to disclosure.
rules.trigger: Time spent reviewing records to determine disclosability
rules.source_language: Fees may not be charged for examination and review to determine if the documents are subject to disclosure.
rules.notes: Fixed $0 for exemption-review labor. Distinguish from redaction, which IS chargeable under SC-0007/SC-0008 — the boundary between reviewing-for-exemption (free) and redacting (chargeable) is a known human-review flag.

rules.legal_concept: Records furnished at lowest possible cost
rules.atomic_rule: Records must be furnished at the lowest possible cost to the person requesting them.
rules.trigger: Furnishing records for a fee
rules.source_language: The records must be furnished at the lowest possible cost to the person requesting the records.
rules.notes: Undefined standard ("lowest possible cost") governing how fees are computed; kept as a soft standard, not converted to a number.

rules.legal_concept: Discretionary fee waiver/reduction in the public interest
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may furnish documents without charge or at a reduced charge where it determines that waiver or reduction is in the public interest because furnishing the information primarily benefits the general public.
rules.trigger: Agency determination that furnishing primarily benefits the general public
rules.source_language: Documents may be furnished when appropriate without charge or at a reduced charge where the agency determines that waiver or reduction of the fee is in the public interest because furnishing the information can be considered as primarily benefiting the general public.
rules.notes: Discretionary branch (waive / reduce / no waiver); the engine must be able to execute a fee-waiver decision path.

rules.legal_concept: No charge to General Assembly members for legislative-duty requests
rules.atomic_rule: Members of the General Assembly may receive copies of records or documents at no charge when the request relates to their legislative duties.
rules.trigger: Requester is a member of the General Assembly and request relates to legislative duties
rules.source_language: However, members of the General Assembly may receive copies of records or documents at no charge from public bodies when their request relates to their legislative duties.
rules.notes: Special-requester-class branch (fee = $0) conditioned on legislative-duty nexus.

rules.legal_concept: Public body must post a fee schedule online
rules.atomic_rule: A public body shall develop a fee schedule and post it online.
rules.trigger: None stated (standing obligation governing fees charged on requests)
rules.source_language: The public body shall develop a fee schedule to be posted online.
rules.notes: Included because the fee applied to an individual request must come from a published schedule; borderline administrative, but directly binds the fee value used in processing.

rules.legal_concept: Deposit up to 25% of anticipated reproduction cost before search/copying
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may require, prior to searching for or making copies of records, a deposit not to exceed twenty-five percent of the total reasonably anticipated cost for reproduction of the records.
rules.trigger: Before the public body searches for or copies records
rules.source_language: A deposit not to exceed twenty-five percent of the total reasonably anticipated cost for reproduction of the records may be required prior to the public body searching for or making copies of records.
rules.notes: Ceiling = 25% of anticipated reproduction cost; city sets whether/how much deposit to require under the cap. When a deposit is required, the production clock runs from deposit receipt (SC-0026).

rules.legal_concept: Full cost due at time of production
rules.atomic_rule: The full amount of the total cost must be paid at the time of the production of the request.
rules.trigger: Production of the requested records
rules.source_language: The full amount of the total cost must be paid at the time of the production of the request.
rules.notes: Payment step gating release; balance beyond any deposit is collected at production.

rules.legal_concept: 10-business-day determination notice
rules.atomic_rule: The public body shall, within ten days (excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and legal public holidays) of receipt of a written request, notify the requester of its determination and the reasons for it.
rules.trigger: Receipt of a written request for records
rules.clock_spec: 10 business-days (excluding Sat/Sun/legal holidays) from receipt of request
rules.source_language: Each public body, upon written request for records made under this chapter, shall within ten days (excepting Saturdays, Sundays, and legal public holidays) of the receipt of the request, notify the person making the request of its determination and the reasons for it; provided, however, that if the record is more than twenty-four months old at the date the request is made, the public body has twenty days (excepting Saturdays, Sundays, and legal public holidays) of the receipt to make this notification.
rules.effective_status: Current (2017 Act No. 67 revised time limits)
rules.notes: Fixed count; the determination notice is a determination of public availability, not necessarily production. Distinct 20-day track for older records at SC-0021.

rules.legal_concept: 20-business-day determination notice for records over 24 months old
rules.atomic_rule: If the record is more than twenty-four months old at the date the request is made, the public body has twenty days (excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and legal public holidays) of receipt to make the determination notification.
rules.trigger: Requested record is more than 24 months old at the date of request
rules.clock_spec: 20 business-days (excluding Sat/Sun/legal holidays) from receipt of request
rules.source_language: provided, however, that if the record is more than twenty-four months old at the date the request is made, the public body has twenty days (excepting Saturdays, Sundays, and legal public holidays) of the receipt to make this notification.
rules.notes: Record-age branch modifying the determination clock; age measured at date of request.

rules.legal_concept: Determination must state reasons
rules.atomic_rule: The determination notice must state the public body's determination and the reasons for it.
rules.trigger: Issuing the determination on a request
rules.source_language: notify the person making the request of its determination and the reasons for it
rules.notes: Content requirement for the notice (a required document element), split from the deadline in SC-0020.

rules.legal_concept: Determination is final opinion on availability but need not resolve redaction
rules.atomic_rule: The determination constitutes the public body's final opinion as to public availability of the requested record, but is not required to include a final decision or opinion on whether specific portions may be subject to redaction under exemptions.
rules.trigger: Issuing the determination on a request
rules.source_language: This determination must constitute the final opinion of the public body as to the public availability of the requested public record, however, the determination is not required to include a final decision or express an opinion as to whether specific portions of the documents or information may be subject to redaction according to exemptions provided for by Section 30-4-40 or other state or federal laws.
rules.notes: Defines what the determination stage must resolve (availability) vs. what it may defer (line-item redaction), which occurs at production.

rules.legal_concept: 30-calendar-day production after determination
rules.atomic_rule: If the request is granted, the record must be furnished or made available for inspection or copying no later than thirty calendar days from the date the final determination was provided.
rules.trigger: Final determination granting the request was provided (and no deposit required)
rules.clock_spec: 30 calendar-days from date final determination was provided
rules.source_language: If the request is granted, the record must be furnished or made available for inspection or copying no later than thirty calendar days from the date on which the final determination was provided, unless the records are more than twenty-four months old, in which case the public body has no later than thirty-five calendar days from the date on which the final determination was provided.
rules.notes: Calendar days (not business days), unlike the determination clock. Applies when no deposit is required; if a deposit is required, the clock runs from deposit receipt (SC-0026).

rules.legal_concept: 35-calendar-day production for records over 24 months old
rules.atomic_rule: If the granted records are more than twenty-four months old, they must be furnished no later than thirty-five calendar days from the date the final determination was provided.
rules.trigger: Granted records are more than 24 months old
rules.clock_spec: 35 calendar-days from date final determination was provided
rules.source_language: unless the records are more than twenty-four months old, in which case the public body has no later than thirty-five calendar days from the date on which the final determination was provided.
rules.notes: Record-age branch on the production clock.

rules.legal_concept: Production clock runs from deposit receipt when deposit required
rules.atomic_rule: If a deposit is required, the record must be furnished or made available no later than thirty calendar days (thirty-five if records are more than 24 months old) from the date the deposit is received.
rules.trigger: A deposit under subsection (B) is required by the public body
rules.clock_spec: 30 calendar-days (35 if records >24 months old) from date deposit is received
rules.source_language: If a deposit as provided in subsection (B) is required by the public body, the record must be furnished or made available for inspection or copying no later than thirty calendar days from the date on which the deposit is received, unless the records are more than twenty-four months old, in which case the public body has no later than thirty-five calendar days from the date on which the deposit was received to fulfill the request.
rules.notes: Alternate start event for the production clock: deposit receipt rather than determination date. Requiring a deposit effectively resets the production start to when the deposit is paid.

rules.legal_concept: Deadlines extendable by written mutual agreement
rules.atomic_rule: The response, determination, and production deadlines may be extended by written mutual agreement of the public body and the requesting party, which agreement shall not be unreasonably withheld.
rules.trigger: Written mutual agreement of the public body and requester
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: extension for the period set by written mutual agreement, from the affected deadline
rules.source_language: The various response, determination, and production deadlines provided by this subsection are subject to extension by written mutual agreement of the public body and the requesting party at issue, and this agreement shall not be unreasonably withheld.
rules.notes: Applies to all § 30-4-30(C) clocks. Extension length is whatever the parties agree — no statutory cap; agreement not to be unreasonably withheld.

rules.legal_concept: Constructive approval on failure to timely notify
rules.atomic_rule: If written notification of the determination is neither mailed, electronically transmitted, nor personally delivered to the requester within the statutory time, the request must be considered approved as to nonexempt records or information.
rules.trigger: No determination notice delivered within the § 30-4-30(C) deadline
rules.clock_spec: Deemed approved upon expiry of the 10/20 business-day determination deadline without notice
rules.source_language: If written notification of the determination of the public body as to the availability of the requested public record is neither mailed, electronically transmitted, nor personally delivered to the person requesting the document within the time set forth by this section, the request must be considered approved as to nonexempt records or information.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: silence = deemed approval (constructive grant), a terminal clock event. Limited to nonexempt records; exemptions survive (SC-0029).

rules.legal_concept: Exemptions not waived by failure to respond
rules.atomic_rule: Exemptions from disclosure under § 30-4-40 or other state/federal law are not waived by the public body's failure to respond within the statutory time.
rules.trigger: Deemed approval arises from non-response
rules.source_language: Exemptions from disclosure as set forth in Section 30-4-40 or by other state or federal laws are not waived by the public body's failure to respond as set forth in this subsection.
rules.notes: Qualifies the deemed-approval trigger: constructive grant reaches only nonexempt material; the body may still withhold exempt records.

rules.legal_concept: Records provided in convenient and practical form when equally convenient for the body
rules.atomic_rule: Records must be provided in a form both convenient and practical for use by the requester, if it is equally convenient for the public body to provide them in that form.
rules.trigger: Requester specifies a form of production
rules.source_language: Records must be provided in a form that is both convenient and practical for use by the person requesting copies of the records concerned, if it is equally convenient for the public body to provide the records in this form.
rules.notes: Format-of-production standard conditioned on "equally convenient" for the body — an undefined standard, kept as source term.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to create a nonexistent electronic version
rules.atomic_rule: A public body is not required to create an electronic version of a public record when one does not exist in order to fulfill a records request.
rules.trigger: Requested electronic version does not exist
rules.source_language: A public body is not required to create an electronic version of a public record when one does not exist to fulfill a records request.
rules.notes: Limits the electronic-transmission right: no obligation to create records that don't exist in electronic form.

rules.legal_concept: Duty to separate exempt from nonexempt and release nonexempt
rules.atomic_rule: If a public record contains material that is not exempt under § 30-4-40(a), the public body shall separate the exempt and nonexempt material and make the nonexempt material available.
rules.trigger: Record contains a mix of exempt and nonexempt material
rules.source_language: If any public record contains material which is not exempt under subsection (a) of this section, the public body shall separate the exempt and nonexempt material and make the nonexempt material available in accordance with the requirements of this chapter.
rules.notes: Segregability/redaction duty. Redaction labor is chargeable (SC-0007/SC-0008) but exemption-review is not (SC-0013).

rules.legal_concept: Enumerated records available in person without a written request
rules.atomic_rule: Specified records (recent meeting minutes; crime/incident reports under § 30-4-50(A)(8) for the prior 14 days; jail/detention/prison confinement documents for the prior 3 months; documents distributed to or reviewed by members during a public meeting for the prior 6 months) must be available for inspection and copying during operating hours, without a written request, when the requester appears in person, unless exempt.
rules.trigger: Requester appears in person during hours of operation seeking an enumerated record
rules.source_language: The following records of a public body must be made available for public inspection and copying during the hours of operations of the public body, unless the record is exempt pursuant to Section 30-4-40 or other state or federal laws, without the requestor being required to make a written request to inspect or copy the records when the requestor appears in person: (1) minutes of the meetings of the public body for the preceding six months; (2) all reports identified in Section 30-4-50(A)(8) for at least the fourteen-day period before the current day; (3) documents identifying persons confined in a jail, detention center, or prison for the preceding three months; and (4) all documents produced by the public body or its agent that were distributed to or reviewed by a member of the public body during a public meeting for the preceding six-month period.
rules.notes: Walk-in immediate-inspection branch that bypasses the written-request/determination-clock path for enumerated record classes and lookback windows.

rules.legal_concept: Website posting deemed compliance with in-person availability
rules.atomic_rule: A public body that places the § 30-4-30(D) records in a convenient and practical form on a publicly available Internet website is deemed compliant with subsection (D), provided it also produces documents on request under the section.
rules.trigger: Enumerated (D) records posted on a public website
rules.source_language: A public body that places the records in a form that is both convenient and practical for use on a publicly available Internet website is deemed to be in compliance with the provisions of subsection (D), provided that the public body also shall produce documents pursuant to this section upon request.
rules.notes: Compliance-by-publication path for the walk-in category; does not relieve the general on-request production duty.

rules.legal_concept: Circuit court declaratory judgment / injunctive relief to enforce FOIA
rules.atomic_rule: A citizen of the State may apply to the circuit court for a declaratory judgment, injunctive relief, or both, to enforce the chapter, if the application is made no later than one year after the alleged violation (or one year after a public vote in public session, whichever is later).
rules.trigger: Alleged FOIA violation; application by a citizen of the State
rules.clock_spec: 1 year (statute of limitations) from date of alleged violation, or from a public vote in public session, whichever is later
rules.source_language: A citizen of the State may apply to the circuit court for a declaratory judgment, injunctive relief, or both, to enforce the provisions of this chapter in appropriate cases if the application is made no later than one year after the date of the alleged violation or one year after a public vote in public session, whichever comes later.
rules.effective_status: Current (2017 Act No. 67 added time constraints)
rules.notes: Enforcement is judicial (circuit court); there is no statutory administrative/internal appeal stage in SC FOIA. Standing here is limited to a "citizen of the State," narrower than the "person" who may request (SC-0001). Namespaced appeal.judicial.* per contract.

rules.legal_concept: Initial hearing scheduled within 10 days of service
rules.atomic_rule: Upon filing of the request for declaratory judgment or injunctive relief, the chief administrative judge of the circuit court must schedule an initial hearing within ten days of service on all parties.
rules.trigger: Filing of a § 30-4-100 request for relief and service on all parties
rules.clock_spec: 10 days from service on all parties (to schedule initial hearing)
rules.source_language: Upon the filing of the request for declaratory judgment or injunctive relief related to provisions of this chapter, the chief administrative judge of the circuit court must schedule an initial hearing within ten days of the service on all parties.
rules.notes: Court-side scheduling deadline within the judicial-appeal path.

rules.legal_concept: Action to conclude within six months of filing absent good cause
rules.atomic_rule: If the court cannot make a final ruling at the initial hearing, it shall set a scheduling order to conclude the action within six months of initial filing; the court may extend this on a showing of good cause.
rules.trigger: No final ruling at the initial hearing
rules.clock_spec: 6 months from initial filing to conclude the action (extendable for good cause)
rules.source_language: If the hearing court is unable to make a final ruling at the initial hearing, the court shall establish a scheduling order to conclude actions brought pursuant to this chapter within six months of initial filing. The court may extend this time period upon a showing of good cause.
rules.notes: Case-conclusion deadline in the judicial-appeal path; good-cause extension available.

rules.legal_concept: Public body may seek court relief from improper requests or on exemption uncertainty
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may file a request for hearing with the circuit court to seek relief from unduly burdensome, overly broad, vague, repetitive, or otherwise improper requests, or where it cannot make a good-faith determination whether information is exempt.
rules.trigger: Request is unduly burdensome/overly broad/vague/repetitive/improper, or the body cannot determine exemption in good faith
rules.source_language: A public body may file a request for hearing with the circuit court to seek relief from unduly burdensome, overly broad, vague, repetitive, or otherwise improper requests, or where it has received a request but it is unable to make a good faith determination as to whether the information is exempt from disclosure.
rules.notes: A state the request may enter: the body routes a burdensome/uncertain request to court rather than answering it directly. "Unduly burdensome / overly broad / vague / repetitive / improper" are undefined standards, kept as source terms.

rules.legal_concept: Third party with specific interest may seek hearing to block disclosure of enumerated exempt records
rules.atomic_rule: If a disclosure request may release records or information exempt under § 30-4-40(a)(1),(2),(4),(5),(9),(14),(15), or (19), a person or entity with a specific interest in the underlying records has the right to request a hearing with the court or to intervene in a previously filed action.
rules.trigger: Request may release records exempt under enumerated § 30-4-40(a) categories and a third party has a specific interest
rules.source_language: If a request for disclosure may result in the release of records or information exempt from disclosure under Section 30-4-40(a)(1), (2), (4), (5), (9), (14), (15), or (19), a person or entity with a specific interest in the underlying records or information shall have the right to request a hearing with the court or to intervene in an action previously filed.
rules.notes: Reverse-FOIA branch: a third-party interest holder can inject a hearing/intervention before enumerated exempt categories are released. Requires human legal review to map which records fall in the enumerated exemptions.

rules.legal_concept: 15-business-day window for agency to seek order barring disclosure of law-enforcement recording
rules.atomic_rule: For disclosure of law-enforcement vehicle-mounted/dashboard recording data of an officer-involved incident resulting in death, injury, property damage, or use of deadly force, the agency may apply to circuit court for a non-disclosure order; the hearing must be requested within fifteen days (excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and legal public holidays) of receipt of the request for disclosure, and the hearing is held in camera.
rules.trigger: Request to disclose qualifying law-enforcement vehicle/dashboard recording data
rules.clock_spec: 15 business-days (excluding Sat/Sun/legal holidays) from receipt of the disclosure request to request a hearing
rules.source_language: A law enforcement or public safety agency may apply to the circuit court for an order to prevent the disclosure of the video or audio recording data. Notice of the request and of the hearing must be provided to the person seeking the record. A hearing must be requested within fifteen days (excepting Saturdays, Sundays, and legal public holidays) of the receipt of the request for disclosure and the hearing shall be held in-camera.
rules.notes: Special-record workflow with its own clock, notice, and in-camera hearing. Court may order withholding only on clear-and-convincing showing under § 30-4-40(a)(3) (see special-records table); may order redacted release.

structural_branches.description: Requester-class gate: incarcerated persons are excluded from the FOIA inspect/copy right (constitutional discovery rights preserved). § 30-4-30(A)(1).

Alternate intake/production path: enumerated record classes (recent minutes, incident reports, confinement docs, meeting-distributed docs, within stated lookback windows) available in person, immediately, without a written request or determination clock. § 30-4-30(D).
Compliance-by-publication branch: posting the (D) records online satisfies the in-person availability duty. § 30-4-30(E).
Terminal state: silence past the 10/20-business-day determination deadline = request deemed approved as to nonexempt records (exemptions not waived). § 30-4-30(C).
Discretionary fee decision path: waive/reduce/charge based on public-interest / primary-benefit-to-general-public finding. § 30-4-30(B).
Special-requester branch: General Assembly members pay no charge for legislative-duty requests. § 30-4-30(B).

SC's only enforcement path is judicial (circuit court declaratory/injunctive), citizen-of-the-State standing, 1-year limit, with statutory 10-day-to-hearing and 6-month-to-conclude court clocks. No administrative/internal appeal exists. § 30-4-100.
Body-initiated diversion path: the public body routes an improper/burdensome request, or one it cannot resolve for exemption, to circuit court instead of answering. § 30-4-110(A).
Reverse-FOIA branch: a third party with a specific interest may demand a hearing/intervene before release of records in enumerated § 30-4-40(a) exempt categories. § 30-4-110(B).

Special-record workflow for law-enforcement vehicle/dashboard recordings of qualifying officer-involved incidents: 15-business-day agency hearing window, notice to requester, in-camera hearing, clear-and-convincing standard. § 30-4-50(A)(9).

material_negatives.note: No separate receipt-acknowledgment requirement distinct from the substantive determination. SC's first statutory duty is the 10-business-day (20 for records >24 months) determination-and-reasons notice under § 30-4-30(C); there is no earlier 'we received your request' acknowledgment obligation. Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

No statewide fixed per-page copy rate. § 30-4-30(B) caps copy fees at the 'prevailing commercial rate' (a ceiling) and requires uniformity, but sets no cents-per-page number; the city supplies the value under the commercial-rate ceiling (see SC-0009).

No statutory duty for the public body to help a requester clarify or narrow a request, and no clarification clock that tolls or restarts the response deadlines. The body's remedy for a vague/overbroad request is to seek a court hearing under § 30-4-110(A) (SC-0038), not a statutory clarify-and-toll mechanism.

No statutory administrative or internal-agency appeal stage, and no AG/records-authority adjudicative review of denials. Enforcement is exclusively judicial via circuit court (§ 30-4-100). The SC Attorney General issues advisory FOIA opinions but has no statutory power to compel disclosure.

No statutorily prescribed request form, portal, or delivery channel. § 30-4-30(C) requires a 'written request' to trigger the response duties but does not mandate a particular medium or form (email, letter, and portal all qualify if written).

No unilateral good-cause extension of the § 30-4-30(C) determination/production clocks by the public body. Extensions require written MUTUAL agreement of the body and requester (SC-0027); the statute provides no body-only extension for volume/complexity.

No statutory rolling/installment production scheme (records produced in tranches with staggered deadlines). The statute sets a single production deadline (30/35 calendar days) from determination or deposit receipt.
